# PRISM window redesign, stage 1 — the look's foundation: Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Give today's window the approved look (colours, lettering, three appearance choices, light figures in the look's line colours) without moving a screen or a word, and put under it what every later stage stands on: the tests moved onto shared helpers, the look's one table, and the painted devices and the shared question class built and tested but mounted on no screen.

**Architecture:** One table of named colours, type and sizes in `core/gui/design.py`; four things read it and nothing else holds a colour or a size: one application style sheet, one palette, one small style over Fusion, and the painted devices (`core/gui/paint.py`, `core/gui/style.py`, `core/gui/widgets/`). Matplotlib's settings are written once, light, when the application is built; the engine's plotting code takes four named colours from one new engine module (engine change E12, the only one of this stage). Every behaviour change is test-first; every task has its own review and one one-process fast gate, started together.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.12, PySide6 6.9.3, matplotlib 3.10.7, torch 2.9.0+cu130, sbi 0.26.1, pytest; the conda env `biophys-env`.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-window-redesign-design.md` (approved 2026-10-06) with its parts in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-window-redesign-design/`: `04-look.md` (the look), `11-engine.md` section 11.14 (E12), `13-tests-stages-docs.md` (the tests, the stages); the locked records `…-assets/decisions-as-approved.md` and `…-assets/rulings-after-the-drafts.md` (the later wins); the built sample `…-assets/toolkit-sample.py.txt`. Read them with this plan: every task cites the sections it implements, and those sections are binding except where "Departures from the design" below says otherwise. The working record of this plan (the reports it was written from, each task's notes for the controller, the ledger) is the gitignored `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-window-redesign/`.

## For the owner: what this plan does, in plain words

**What you have at its end.** The window you know, with every screen, tab, button and word where it is today, in the new colours and lettering. Three appearance choices (Follow Windows, Light, Dark). Every figure PRISM draws on a white page, its named lines in the colour-blind-safe colours. Questions are still today's boxes. Underneath, not yet on any screen: the markers, the ruled table, the time axis, the page pieces, the number boxes that write 20,480,000, and the one question dialog, each built and tested, ready for stage 2 onward.

**How big it is.** Nineteen building tasks and four that I run myself, where the design guessed eleven. Three reasons: moving the 322 window tests onto shared helpers is four tasks on its own; the painted pieces are six; and two tasks were cut in two so that a failing test run points at one cause. Each building task ends with a review and one full run of the fast tests (about 17 minutes), so the test runs alone are about six hours of machine time, spread over several sessions.

**What needs your hand.**
1. *About ten minutes with Windows' text-size slider* (Settings, Accessibility, Text size: up to 150 %, later back to 100 %), at a moment we agree on with nothing running. It tells me whether the toolkit already follows that setting. For about five of those minutes everything on your screen is at 150 %. If you would rather not, there is a fallback that needs nothing from you.
2. *Looking at pictures, twice.* After the tenth task the window first wears the whole new look: I will show you every screen in light and dark then, so that anything you dislike is changed before more is built on it. And again at the end of the stage, as you asked.

**What I will do on your computer beyond editing code and running tests.** At three moments (when this plan is committed, after the tenth task, at the end) I build the real window, hidden, to take its pictures: a few short runs each time. One test does the same after the eighth and tenth tasks and at the end, to see the lettering as Windows really draws it. Each uses a scratch settings file and an empty scratch record store, never yours, and reads the graphics card's free memory as the window always does; I will not do it while anything of yours is running. Once, after the second task, I break three lines of the program by hand to see that the moved tests still catch a fault, then put them back; nothing of that is committed. At the end of the stage the slow tests run for about 75 minutes on the card; I will tell you before I start them.

**Choices in this plan that you have not seen.** Approving the plan approves these unless you strike one. The ones that change what you would notice:
- *The order inside the stage is not the design's.* The two ticks in Settings ("Use the Windows accent colour", "Use the Inter font everywhere") and "Auto (time of day)" go before the lettering and the colours change, because those steps remove what the ticks act on. Everything the design lists for this stage is still delivered.
- *On your own computer the window will open dark after the appearance task.* Your saved choice is "Auto (time of day)", which goes; it is then read as "Follow Windows", and Windows is in dark mode here. The accent returns from Windows' colour to PRISM's blue. One click in Settings picks Light.
- *A comma typed in a number box is no longer turned into another number.* Today, typing 6,5 into a decimal box silently becomes 65 (measured; the memory-limit box among them). After the number-box task, in a box that takes a decimal the comma stays where you typed it, the box is outlined, and the run is refused in words until it is corrected. A whole-number box does not take the comma key at all (typing 5,000 shows 5000 as you type) and no longer accepts a leading "+". This reaches today's forms at once; the commas that group thousands still arrive page by page, as you chose.
- *The mouse wheel over a closed drop-down list no longer changes its choice.* It is not in the design. Today, scrolling a form with the pointer over a drop-down silently changes a setting.
- *The keyboard-focus ring appears on every control* of today's forms from the tenth task: after Tab or a shortcut, and after a click only in a box one types in. A list or a scrolling area shows it just inside its edge.
- *How today's forms look in the new colours* until each is rebuilt: a group of settings is marked by a thin grey frame on the white page; a greyed tab or control is less grey than today (the design makes disabled text readable on purpose); the drop-downs still have no arrow, as today; menus are drawn like tool tips. You judge these from the pictures after the tenth task.
- *Console text* (a record's text, for now) is set in Cascadia Mono, as you chose; the log pane keeps its face until the stage that rebuilds it.
- *Figures.* Beyond the white page and the named colours you approved: a figure's unnamed lines now take the seven colours in turn, so in the window the observation's trace and the corner plot's histograms turn from blue to ink, and its truth mark from orange to blue; the three calibration figures the fitting library draws itself keep that library's dark red, pure blue and grey, which PRISM's code cannot reach.
- *On a computer with neither Cambria nor Georgia* the program's sentences are set in Inter at the sentence size, not at the smaller body size.
- *No row for you to run on a real screen is written in this stage.* The first rows' words name pages that later stages build; they are written when they can be run.

The full list, with what each costs if it is wrong, is "Departures from the design" below. Appendix A, at the end of this file, says task by task what you would notice and lists every choice in that task that you have not seen, in plain words. Also: the look's two added colours are sky blue #56B4E9 and purple #CC79A7 (on a dark page the two blues change places, as the accent does).

**What does not change.** No model, simulation, feature, training or calibration method; nothing in `core/config.py`; no setting's meaning; no simulation set's identity; nothing under `Artifacts/`; nothing the window remembers except that the two removed ticks stop being read and a saved "Auto (time of day)" is read as "Follow Windows". `CLAUDE.md` is not edited: two of its counts (the test suites, the session guards) will be one short after this stage, and I will put corrected wording to you at the stage's end.

## Global Constraints

- **Interpreter.** `C:\Users\J\anaconda3\envs\biophys-env\python.exe` (in Bash: `/c/Users/J/anaconda3/envs/biophys-env/python.exe`); the `python` on PATH is another interpreter with none of the dependencies. The root `conftest.py` defaults `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` and `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE` for pytest; a bare script sets what it needs. A foreground check that imports torch can hang: write it to a script and run it with a timeout.
- **Git.** The local `main`; one commit per task (a fix after review is its own commit), never amended; a short subject; the message ends with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; `git add` each changed file by name; read `git status` first; undo with `git stash`, never `git checkout -- <file>`. The owner pushes.
- **Suites.** Never edit a file under `core/`, `tests/` or the root `conftest.py` while a pytest process is alive; never two pytest processes. An implementer runs only its focused tests (one file or a few tests, one process; in the background with a log when a run can pass ten minutes). The controller runs each task's fast gate (`python -m pytest -m "not slow" -q --durations=10`, one process, background, logged) and starts it with the task's review. Reviewers are read-only and run no pytest.
- **Scope.** Stage 1 touches no engine file but the eight of Task 12, nothing in `core/config.py`, no refusal key (`core.refusals.FIELDS` stays at 109), nothing a simulated row holds, no simulation set's identity, no record on disk, and nothing the window remembers except: the two appearance keys stop being read and a stored "auto" reads as "system". A seed, a name, a note and a consent are never remembered. A whole number that an older build stored with its commas is read as that number and saved back without them. No screen's words change but these: the appearance choices (three, the first named "Follow Windows"; "Auto (time of day)", the two ticks and the note under them go: Task 7) and one new tool tip on a number box in error, "Use a point as the decimal sign." (Task 17). If a task turns out to need more of the engine, STOP and report.
- **Dialogs.** Every modal dialog is an INSTANCE (`QMessageBox(...)`, a `QDialog` instance), never a static call; the session guards depend on it. The one exception is a file chooser: the two static calls inside `core/gui/file_chooser.choose_file` (Task 4), which a session guard of their own records (Task 1). A real `exec()` of a dialog off-screen stalls the run: a test opens a dialog without blocking and sends keys, or goes through the guard.
- **Knobs.** Every knob reaches its stage as an argument; no task writes `core.config`.
- **THE REFERENCE RULE.** Nothing written into `core/`, `tests/`, `conftest.py`, `README.md` or `docs/guide/` (code, comment, docstring, on-screen string, test name) may cite a working document or its labels: no design id (U6, E12, B19, C20, D1, W080, G7 and the like: `tests/test_source_hygiene.py` refuses any lone capital letter with one to three digits, "C0" to "C9" and SVG path letters included), no "ruling" (say rule, rules, ruled), no "this/each/next/earlier piece" (say device or part), no "Task N", "section N.M", "walkthrough", "ledger", "STATE.md", "CLAUDE.md", "finding N", "the review of", "Appendix". Also forbidden by the owner though no scan catches them: "part 4", "stage 1", "item 7", "the design", "the sample", "the mock-up", any plug-in's name. Say the reason in words. Test names: no token of one letter plus one to three digits between underscores (`f1`, `e12`, `c10`), none of ruling, walkthrough, handoff, appendix. Six-digit colours in capitals pass. This plan may use the ids; the code it dictates may not.
- **Two scans a new module can trip.** Under `core/`, a string literal passed to ANY call as a keyword named `field` or `key`, or as the first argument of anything named `describe` or `refuse`, must be a registered refusal key (name parameters `name`, `kind`, `role`); no call to a bare name `input`.
- **No torch in the look.** The look's modules and `tests/test_look.py` import no torch: `core.gui.design`, `fonts`, `theming`, `mpl_theme`, `settings`, `paint`, `style`, `file_chooser`, `widgets.labeled_inputs` and the new widget modules, `core.Helpers.plot_colours`. None may import `core.gui.fields`, `core.config`, `core.registry` or `core.Helpers.file_manager`. `tests/test_look.py` does not import `tests/_fixtures.py` (it imports torch); it gets its application object from `QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])`. It must not contain the text `use_ini_file(None)`. A new look module is added to `LOOK_MODULES`, whose one fresh-interpreter test proves the whole list loads no torch; no later task writes its own probe of that. Five tests start an interpreter of their own for another reason and stay: Task 4's (before the list exists), Task 12's (neither torch nor matplotlib), Task 2's (its module is not a look module), Task 8's (the state with no application object) and Task 13's (a child ended on purpose).
- **ONE application serves the whole gate**, and `tests/test_look.py` is collected before six window suites. In that file:
  - the application object first, before any widget (a widget with no application ends the interpreter with no traceback);
  - never a bare `show()`: where a device must be shown, `Qt.WA_DontShowOnScreen` and `Qt.WA_ShowWithoutActivating` first, never `activateWindow()` or `raise_()`, closed and let go in a `finally`;
  - a widget a test made is let go by dropping its last name or by delivering its own deferred delete (`deleteLater()` then `QCoreApplication.sendPostedEvents(widget, QEvent.DeferredDelete)`); never a bare `deleteLater()`, never a flush of every receiver's deferred deletes;
  - a painter on a picture is ended in a `finally` (a raise under a live painter ends the pytest process with no summary);
  - a palette, sheet, font, style, event filter or colour scheme on the application, `design.set_dark`, `design.set_text_scale`, the default locale and any matplotlib setting only inside a helper or a `finally` that puts each back; `PrismStyle` goes on a widget, not on the application;
  - for the four scalings draw into a `QImage` whose device pixel ratio is set (size rounded up); `QT_SCALE_FACTOR` is per process; no assertion reads the pixels of lettering (off-screen there are no system fonts: every face resolves to Inter);
  - before adding a helper, a fixture or a constant, search the file for its name (a second module-level definition replaces the first for every test above it), and run the WHOLE file before the commit.
- **Process-wide state.** A task that adds something to the application or the process when the whole program is built (a style, a font, a text factor, figure settings, an event filter) adds a key to `process_state(app)` and a line to `whole_program()` in the same commit.
- **The carried-over list** (`.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-window-redesign/carried-over.md`, one row per window test) is kept current by the controller after every task: the names from `git diff` of the test files, the kind of change from the task's report; a test added, renamed ("rewritten (to <new name>)") or retired gets its row in the task that does it.
- **Scratch.** Scratch scripts, the gate script and the picture script live under `C:\Users\J\AppData\Local\Temp\prism-redesign-scratch\`; no `.py` under `.superpowers/` or `docs/`.
- **Qt facts.** The Qt Development Skills plug-in is not used, nor any part of it; what Qt can do is checked in the installed PySide6 6.9.3 or Qt's public documentation, with a scratch script.
- **Kept on disk.** Nothing under `Artifacts/` and not `C:\Users\J\prism-retrain-console.log` is renamed, rewritten, deleted or trained on. No training of real size is started.
- **Real platform.** A step that runs on the real platform (a display-marked test, a picture script) creates hidden windows only, never activates one, and runs with no long run live and no other pytest alive. Building PRISM's whole window reads the card's free memory.

## Review Focus

Conditions the design implies and a person will meet, each pinned by a test in the task that owns the code:

1. **A computer without the chosen faces** (Cascadia Mono on some Windows 10; Cambria and Georgia off Windows): console text and the program's sentences fall back in the stated order and nothing fails — Task 8 (`book_family` and the fixed-width order from lists that lack each face in turn).
2. **Windows' text size above 100 %, up to 225 %, on a small screen**: the window still opens no larger than the screen, and Qt accepts the style sheet built at that factor — Task 6 (`window_sizes` at 2.25 on 1366 x 768) and Task 9 (both sheets taken with no warning at factors 1.0 and 2.25).
3. **A settings file from an older build, or a garbled one** (a stored "auto", an empty or mis-cased word, the two removed keys): PRISM opens on "Follow Windows" or the stored light or dark, crashes on nothing and rewrites nothing before a choice is made — Task 7.
4. **Text that looks like markup** (a path, a record's name or an engine's sentence holding "<", "&", a brace or a line break): shown as written in a sentence, a message row and a question — Tasks 16 and 18; and a question with a 600-character sentence or 200 items stays inside the screen — Task 18.
5. **A display scaling the pictures did not cover** (175 %, 250 %): a painted rule is never zero device pixels — Task 13; **and a character Inter lacks** in a figure's label is drawn, with no missing-glyph warning — Task 11b.

### Files outside the repository that the plan leans on

All under `C:\Users\J\AppData\Local\Temp\prism-redesign-scratch\`. Windows may empty that folder: each
row says what the file computes, so that it can be written again there (never under `.superpowers/` or
`docs/`).

| file | used by | what it computes |
|---|---|---|
| `gate.sh <kind> <label>` | written by 0; every gate; 10p; 19 | starts ONE pytest process and logs it to `stage-1/gates/<kind>-<label>.log`. Kinds: `fast` (`-m "not slow" -q --durations=10`), `quiet` (the same with `--durations=15`; the two gates of record), `slow` (`-m slow -q --durations=5`), `display` (`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows`, `-m display -q`), `collect` (`--collect-only -q`). Refuses (exit 2) on an unknown kind, a missing label, a log that exists, while any `python.exe` is alive, or when `QT_QPA_PLATFORM`, `QT_SCALE_FACTOR`, `PRISM_ARTIFACTS` or `PRISM_RESOURCES` is set |
| `pictures.py <set> [--text-factor F] [--scale S]` | written by 0; run by 0, 10p, 19 | builds the REAL window (imports torch, reads the card's free memory), hidden and never activated, under a scratch settings file and an empty scratch store that it checks before it builds anything; takes the appearance modes from `theming.MODE_LABELS` as it finds them; pictures every screen and tab in each mode, the lower half of each scrolling form, the gear's menu and the smallest window; leaves by `os._exit(0)`; judged by its last printed line and its files ("the nine checks of a picture run", Task 0 Step 10) |
| `compare_page.py` | written by 10p; run by 10p, 19 | standard library, about thirty lines: one HTML page that puts two picture sets side by side |
| `task01_unread_imports.py` | 1 | for each test module, marks every module-level `core.gui` import statement `UNREAD` or `READ` by `ast` and `symtable`; totals (26 unread before Task 1, 0 after) |
| `task01_test_names.py [--check <list>]` | 0, 1, the per-task loop, 19 | the test functions of the nine window suites and the items each collects (`TOTAL <f> functions, <i> items`; 322 and 340 today); with `--check` holds them against the first two cells of the carried-over list's rows and prints `rows <n>; twice [...]; missing <n>: [...]; gone <k>: [...]` |
| `task02_assert_counts_r2.py <base>` | 2 | for five suites, against a base commit: top-level definitions added and removed, definitions whose count of `assert` statements changed, functions that import `QMessageBox` and never read it; last line `differences to explain: <n>` (the older `task02_assert_counts.py` beside it must not be used) |
| `task03_sites.py`, `task03_unread_after_move.py`, `task03_local_imports.py`, `task03r_patch_before_build.py` | 3b | the hand-written construction sites; the import lines the move leaves unread; the imports made inside functions (the baseline of Steps 1 and 5); what a test replaces before it builds |

## How to run this plan

- **The plan is committed at planning time**; the tree is clean before Task 0. Any later correction of the plan by the controller is its own commit.
- **Execution order**: 0, 1, 2, 3a, 3b, 4, 11a, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 10p, 11b, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19. The sections below stand in that order. Task 5 (the owner's hand) runs at the first quiet moment after Task 0 and at the latest before Task 6; Task 6 is not dispatched before it, or before the owner chooses the fallback. Task numbers follow the first draft of the plan, so 11a stands before 6 and 5 may float.
- **Controller tasks** (0, 5, 10p, 19, Step 12 of Task 1 and Step 10 of Task 2) are run by the controller, not an implementer. Their sections cite "ruling B3", "B4", "B7", "D5", "D18" and the like: those are the PLAN's own rulings, `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-window-redesign/stage-1/plan-rulings.md`; "the design's ruling D4" and the like are the design's (`rulings-after-the-drafts.md`).
- **Each task's section is self-contained**: its Binding block restates every rule it can break, because its implementer sees only that section, this head and the design.
- **The per-task loop (the owner's rule).** On an implementer's DONE: check that no python process is alive, start the task's one-process fast gate in the background, and dispatch the task's reviewer at the same moment. Reviewers are read-only and run no pytest. A task is complete when its review is clean AND its gate is green. If the review sends fixes, wait for the gate to exit before any source edit, then fix, re-review the fix commit and start a fresh gate on the fixed head. From Task 6 on a task starts when its predecessor's review is clean, not only when its gate is green: the tasks share `tests/test_look.py`. Task 9's review is done by two readers (the apply and the whole-program test; the table of rules and the token names).
- **After each gate**: tree clean; the real `Artifacts/` unchanged; no `sbi-logs/`; `Resources/Models` holds `SHM.json` and `SHM2.json` only; the gate's line in the ledger with its count and time, and a word on any change in either.
- **Reading Task 8's gate**: a failure in a window suite that PASSES in a one-file run is the face (from that task four suites measure their widgets in Inter); one that fails alone too is the window's size or the product.
- **The owner's hand**: Task 5 (the text-size slider, twice) and the pictures of Task 10p and Task 19 (shown, then the owner's remarks ruled). The owner is told before the slow set at the exit.
- **When what is built departs from the design**: say so in the task's report; the controller asks the owner if it touches something the owner decided, and adds a row to "Departures from the design" here, in the design and in the ledger, with what it costs if it is wrong.
- **The ledger** is `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-window-redesign/progress.md`, with each task's brief, report, review and gate log beside it, as the earlier pieces kept theirs; `docs/STATE.md` is updated at the end of every session and lists E12 when Task 12 lands.

  ```bash
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  # Usage: gate.sh <kind> <label>
  #   kind   fast     a task's one-process fast gate:           pytest -m "not slow" -q --durations=10
  #          quiet    a gate of record, run alone:              pytest -m "not slow" -q --durations=15
  #          slow     the slow set:                             pytest -m slow -q --durations=5
  #          display  the tests that need a real screen:        QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows pytest -m display -q
  #          collect  the list of collected ids:                pytest --collect-only -q
  #   label  the task and the commit, e.g. task00-a1b2c3d (a gate after a fix: task07-fix1-a1b2c3d)
  # One pytest process, logged to <workspace>/stage-1/gates/<kind>-<label>.log. Start it in the background.
  kind=$1
  label=$2
  repo=/c/Users/J/PycharmProjects/PRISM
  gates="$repo/.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-06-window-redesign/stage-1/gates"
  py=/c/Users/J/anaconda3/envs/biophys-env/python.exe
  log="$gates/${kind}-${label}.log"

  case "$kind" in
    fast)    args=(-m "not slow" -q --durations=10) ;;
    quiet)   args=(-m "not slow" -q --durations=15) ;;
    slow)    args=(-m slow -q --durations=5) ;;
    display) args=(-m display -q) ;;
    collect) args=(--collect-only -q) ;;
    *) echo "unknown kind '$kind' (fast, quiet, slow, display, collect)"; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  [ -n "$label" ] || { echo "no label"; exit 2; }
  cd "$repo" || exit 2
  [ -e "$log" ] && { echo "the log exists already: $log"; exit 2; }
  if tasklist //FI "IMAGENAME eq python.exe" //NH 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "python.exe"; then
    echo "a python process is alive; never two pytest processes"; exit 2
  fi
  for name in QT_QPA_PLATFORM QT_SCALE_FACTOR PRISM_ARTIFACTS PRISM_RESOURCES; do
    [ -z "${!name}" ] || { echo "$name is set to '${!name}'; unset it first"; exit 2; }
  done
  [ "$kind" = display ] && export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=windows
  mkdir -p "$gates"

  {
    echo "HEAD $(git rev-parse --short HEAD)  kind $kind  start $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')"
    echo "ENV PRISM_VRAM_CEILING_GIB='${PRISM_VRAM_CEILING_GIB}' PRISM_MEM_LOG_EVERY='${PRISM_MEM_LOG_EVERY}' QT_QPA_PLATFORM='${QT_QPA_PLATFORM}'"
    git status --porcelain
  } > "$log"
  start=$(date +%s)
  "$py" -m pytest "${args[@]}" >> "$log" 2>&1
  rc=$?
  end=$(date +%s)
  echo "EXIT $rc  elapsed $((end-start)) s  end $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')" >> "$log"
  exit $rc
  ```

- [ ] **Step 7: The guard.** Both files before any run. `tests/_fixtures.py`: add `from typing import NamedTuple` after `from pathlib import Path` (`:24`); in the module docstring (`:13-14`) "and the dialog record ``SHOWN`` that tests/conftest.py's session guard appends to" becomes "and the two records tests/conftest.py's session guards append to, the dialogs in ``SHOWN`` and the file choosers in ``CHOOSER_CALLS``" (re-wrap the paragraph, `:12-16`; its sentence on the one import spelling stays word for word); after `SHOWN: list = []` (`:60`):
  ```python
  class ChooserCall(NamedTuple):
      """One file chooser the code under test opened: "save" or "open", the title, the start value and
      the filter it was handed, and the path the test answered with. ``answer`` is "" when the test
      answered by cancelling and None when no test answered at all."""
      kind: str
      title: str
      start: str
      filter: str
      answer: str | None


  # Every file chooser opened since the test began, in order. tests/conftest.py::_no_file_choosers puts
  # chooser_guard in place of QFileDialog.getSaveFileName and getOpenFileName for the session, and
  # _every_file_chooser_is_answered empties this list around each test and fails the test at teardown
  # when it holds a call nobody answered.
  CHOOSER_CALLS: list = []
  _CHOOSER_ANSWER: dict = {}       # {"path": str} while a test's answer_chooser is in force


  def chooser_guard(kind: str):
      """The stand-in for one of QFileDialog's two file-name statics; ``kind`` is "save" or "open".

      It RECORDS the call in CHOOSER_CALLS and returns ``(path, "")``: the path a test gave with
      answer_chooser, or "" -- what Cancel returns -- when no test answered. It never raises: a chooser
      is opened from a clicked slot, and an exception raised inside a slot does not reach the test that
      clicked. An unanswered chooser is reported by check_choosers_answered at the test's teardown.

      A ``staticmethod``, as the entry it replaces is. The parameter names are Qt's own keywords, and
      whatever follows the filter is accepted and ignored: matplotlib's toolbar in a popped-out figure
      passes a selected filter as well."""
      def stand_in(parent=None, caption="", dir="", filter="", *rest, **more):
          answer = _CHOOSER_ANSWER.get("path")
          CHOOSER_CALLS.append(ChooserCall(kind, str(caption), str(dir), str(filter), answer))
          return (answer or "", "")
      return staticmethod(stand_in)


  def answer_chooser(monkeypatch, path: str) -> None:
      """Answer the next file chooser this test opens, and every later one, with ``path``. "" is the
      operator cancelling, and counts as an answer. Undone with the test's ``monkeypatch``; a second
      call replaces the answer."""
      monkeypatch.setitem(_CHOOSER_ANSWER, "path", str(path))


  def check_choosers_answered() -> None:
      """Fail when CHOOSER_CALLS holds a chooser no test answered, naming each one's kind and title.
      Raised rather than asserted, so the check survives a run with assertions switched off."""
      unanswered = [c for c in CHOOSER_CALLS if c.answer is None]
      if unanswered:
          raise AssertionError(
              "a file chooser was opened that this test did not answer (it was recorded and returned "
              "as cancelled): " + "; ".join(f"{c.kind} '{c.title}'" for c in unanswered)
              + ". Answer it before the click with tests._fixtures.answer_chooser(monkeypatch, path); "
                "pass \"\" for a cancel.")
  ```
  (`tests/_fixtures.py` is not a module pytest rewrites, so a bare `assert` there is compiled away under `python -O`; `:523` and `:816` are helpers' own checks, this one is a guard.)
  `tests/conftest.py`, appended after `_clear_shown`:

  ```python
      getSaveFileName and getOpenFileName, are tests/_fixtures.chooser_guard: the call is recorded in
      CHOOSER_CALLS and returns as cancelled unless the test answered it with answer_chooser. A test's

      The save button of matplotlib's toolbar in a popped-out figure calls the same getSaveFileName,
  ```

- What `_read` gives for an unshown `QMessageBox` (the tests of Step 2 hold its values):

| field | rule |
|---|---|
| answer buttons | `box.buttons()` without those whose `buttonRole` is `ActionRole` |
| a button's words | `text()` with `&&` read as `&` and a single `&` removed |
| `safe` | the only answer button; else the single `RejectRole` one; else the single `NoRole` one; else `None`. No answer button at all: `"OK"` |
| `answers` | the other answer buttons in `buttons()`'s order, then the safe one LAST; `("OK",)` when there is none |
| `default` | the words of `defaultButton()` when it is an answer button; else the one answer when there is exactly one; else `None` |
| `marker` | icon `Warning` "warn", `Critical` "err", `Information` "info", any other "" |
| `kind` | the first that holds: two or more answers "question"; icon `Critical` "error"; title "Check your inputs" "refusal"; else "notice" |
| `title`, `sentence`, `beneath`, `detail` | `windowTitle()`, `text()`, `informativeText()`, `detailedText()`, as set |
| `items`, `loses_work` | `()`; True when an answer button has `DestructiveRole` |
| `text` (property) | the non-empty ones of `items` and `beneath`, joined by `"\n"` |

  ```python
  def _raw_box(icon, title, text, *, beneath="", detail="", standard=None, added=(), default=None):
      """An unshown QMessageBox built the way the window builds each of its shapes."""
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox
      box = QMessageBox()
      box.setIcon(icon)
      box.setWindowTitle(title)
      box.setText(text)
      if beneath:
          box.setInformativeText(beneath)
      if detail:
          box.setDetailedText(detail)
      if standard is not None:
          box.setStandardButtons(standard)
      made = {words: box.addButton(words, role) for words, role in added}
      if default is not None:
          box.setDefaultButton(made.get(default, default))
      return box


  def _close_answers():
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox as B
      return (("Cancel task && quit", B.AcceptRole), ("Quit anyway", B.DestructiveRole),
              ("Don't quit", B.RejectRole))


  def test_asked_reads_each_shape_of_box_into_one_record():
      """Every shape of box the window builds, never shown, read into the same record of words."""
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox as B
      from tests._fixtures import Asked, all_asked, asked, forget_asked

      qt_app()
      assert "exec" in B.__dict__, \
          "the session guard is not in force: a raw exec() would stall the run"
      tb = "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  ...\nRuntimeError: it failed"
      noted = "A cancel was requested before the run failed."
      held = "This session holds:\n  a prior\n\nEvery one of them STAYS ON DISK."
      two = (("Apply and start a new session", B.DestructiveRole), ("Keep this session", B.RejectRole))
      one = dict(items=(), answers=("OK",), default="OK", safe="OK", loses_work=False)
      refusal = dict(kind="refusal", title="Check your inputs", marker="warn", detail="", **one)
      error = dict(kind="error", title="Error", marker="err", sentence="it failed", **one)
      session = dict(kind="question", title="Start a new session?", marker="warn", sentence="Replace it?",
                     beneath=held, items=(), detail="", safe="Keep this session", loses_work=True,
                     answers=("Apply and start a new session", "Keep this session"))
      shapes = [
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Check your inputs", "It is blank.", beneath="Set it in the box.",
                    standard=B.Ok, default=B.Ok),
           Asked(sentence="It is blank.", beneath="Set it in the box.", **refusal)),
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Check your inputs", "No cache.", standard=B.Ok, default=B.Ok),
           Asked(sentence="No cache.", beneath="", **refusal)),
          (_raw_box(B.Critical, "Error", "it failed", detail=tb),          # only "Show Details..."
           Asked(beneath="", detail=tb, **error)),
          (_raw_box(B.Critical, "Error", "it failed"),                     # no button at all
           Asked(beneath="", detail="", **error)),
          (_raw_box(B.Critical, "Error", "it failed", beneath=noted, detail=tb),
           Asked(beneath=noted, detail=tb, **error)),
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Cannot edit model", "Could not load 'M':\nbad", standard=B.Ok),
           Asked(kind="notice", title="Cannot edit model", marker="warn",
                 sentence="Could not load 'M':\nbad", beneath="", detail="", **one)),
          (_raw_box(B.Information, "A task is running", "Wait for it.", standard=B.Ok),
           Asked(kind="notice", title="A task is running", marker="info", sentence="Wait for it.",
                 beneath="", detail="", **one)),
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Delete model", "Delete 'M'?", beneath="This removes its files.",
                    standard=B.Yes | B.No, default=B.No),
           Asked(kind="question", title="Delete model", marker="warn", sentence="Delete 'M'?",
                 beneath="This removes its files.", items=(), detail="", answers=("Yes", "No"),
                 default="No", safe="No", loses_work=False)),
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Start a new session?", "Replace it?", beneath=held, added=two,
                    default="Keep this session"),
           Asked(default="Keep this session", **session)),
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "Start a new session?", "Replace it?", beneath=held, added=two),
           Asked(default=None, **session)),                                # never a guessed default
          (_raw_box(B.Warning, "A task is still running", "A task is still running.",
                    beneath="Cancelling stops it at its next checkpoint.", added=_close_answers(),
                    default="Cancel task && quit"),
           Asked(kind="question", title="A task is still running", marker="warn",
                 sentence="A task is still running.",
                 beneath="Cancelling stops it at its next checkpoint.", items=(), detail="",

                 default="Cancel task & quit", safe="Don't quit", loses_work=True)),
      ]
      forget_asked()

          assert box.exec() == 0 and box.clickedButton() is None      # recorded, shown to nobody
      got = all_asked()
      assert len(got) == len(shapes) == 11

  def test_asked_fails_in_words_on_nothing_and_forgetting_empties_the_one_list():
      """One list whichever module names it; a record is the words the box had when it was opened."""
      import pytest
      import tests._dialogs as dialogs
      import tests._fixtures as fixtures
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox

      qt_app()
      assert "exec" in QMessageBox.__dict__, \
          "the session guard is not in force: a raw exec() would stall the run"
      assert fixtures.SHOWN is dialogs.SHOWN and fixtures.CHOOSER_CALLS is dialogs.CHOOSER_CALLS
      for name in ("Asked", "record", "asked", "all_asked", "forget_asked", "choose", "answer_chooser"):
          assert getattr(fixtures, name) is getattr(dialogs, name), name
      assert dialogs.all_asked() == []
      with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="no box was shown"):
          dialogs.asked()
      held = dialogs.SHOWN
      first, second = QMessageBox(), QMessageBox()
      first.setText("one")
      second.setText("two")
      assert first.exec() == 0 and second.exec() == 0
      assert held == [first, second], "the list still holds the boxes themselves, in order"
      assert [a.sentence for a in dialogs.all_asked()] == ["one", "two"] and dialogs.asked().sentence == "two"
      second.setText("changed after it was opened")
      assert dialogs.asked().sentence == "two"
      dialogs.forget_asked()
      assert dialogs.all_asked() == [] and held == [] and dialogs.SHOWN is held, \
          "forgetting must empty the one list in place"
      with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="not a message box"):
          dialogs.record(object())
      assert held == [], "what could not be read must not be kept"
      held.append(QMessageBox())                       # by hand, past the guard
      with pytest.raises(AssertionError, match="by hand"):
          dialogs.all_asked()
      dialogs.forget_asked()


  def test_choose_clicks_the_answer_it_was_given_and_a_box_without_it_takes_its_safe_one(monkeypatch):
      """An answer is a CLICK on the box's own button, which is how the window reads one."""
      import pytest
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox as B
      from tests._fixtures import all_asked, choose, forget_asked

      qt_app()
      assert "exec" in B.__dict__, \
          "the session guard is not in force: a raw exec() would stall the run"

      def clicked(which):
          if which == "yes or no":
              box = _raw_box(B.Warning, "Delete model", "Delete 'M'?", standard=B.Yes | B.No, default=B.No)
          elif which == "close":
              box = _raw_box(B.Warning, "A task is still running", "A task is still running.",
                             added=_close_answers(), default="Cancel task && quit")
          elif which == "refused":
              box = _raw_box(B.Warning, "Check your inputs", "It is blank.", standard=B.Ok, default=B.Ok)
          else:
              box = _raw_box(B.Critical, "Error", "it failed")
          got = box.exec()
          pressed = box.clickedButton()
          return got, (None if pressed is None else pressed.text())

      # the other answer: the one that is not the safe one, on a box with exactly two
      counts = []
      forget_asked()
      choose(monkeypatch, other=True, during=lambda: counts.append(len(all_asked())))
      assert clicked("yes or no") == (B.Yes, "&Yes"), "the window reads this box as exec() == Yes"
      assert clicked("refused") == (0, None), "one answer: there is no other, so it stays unanswered"
      assert clicked("failed") == (0, None)
      assert clicked("close") == (0, None), "three answers: 'the other' names none of them"
      assert counts == [1, 2, 3, 4], "recorded first, then `during`, then the click"

      # by its words as shown: no mnemonic mark, a doubled one read as one
      for words, raw in (("Cancel task & quit", "Cancel task && quit"), ("Quit anyway", "Quit anyway"),
                         ("Don't quit", "Don't quit")):
          choose(monkeypatch, words=words)
          assert clicked("close")[1] == raw, words
      choose(monkeypatch, words="No such answer")
      assert clicked("close") == (0, None)
      choose(monkeypatch, words="Yes")
      assert clicked("yes or no")[0] == B.Yes

      # the default, as Enter presses it; a box whose code set none stays unanswered
      choose(monkeypatch, default=True)
      assert clicked("yes or no") == (B.No, "&No") and clicked("close")[1] == "Cancel task && quit"
      assert clicked("failed") == (0, None)

      # nothing chosen is the unanswered guard again, still recorded; and one way of choosing at most
      choose(monkeypatch)
      before = len(all_asked())
      assert clicked("yes or no") == (0, None) and len(all_asked()) == before + 1
      for bad in (dict(words="Yes", other=True), dict(other=True, default=True)):
          with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="at most one"):
              choose(monkeypatch, **bad)
      monkeypatch.undo()
      assert clicked("yes or no") == (0, None) and len(all_asked()) == before + 2, \
          "the session guard must be back after the undo"

  _RAW_BOX_READS = ("informativeText", "detailedText", "defaultButton", "standardButtons", "buttonRole",
                    "clickedButton", "escapeButton")
  _MAY_HOLD_A_RAW_BOX = frozenset({
      "test_an_unexpected_modal_is_recorded_in_shown_and_returns_zero",
      "test_asked_reads_each_shape_of_box_into_one_record",
      "test_asked_fails_in_words_on_nothing_and_forgetting_empties_the_one_list",
      "test_choose_clicks_the_answer_it_was_given_and_a_box_without_it_takes_its_safe_one",
  })


  def _direct_box_reads(source: str) -> list[tuple[int, str, str]]:
      """``(line, top-level definition, what)`` for every place a module names the recorded list, reads
      an attribute only a message box has, or replaces ``QMessageBox.exec``. Parsed, so a comment or a
      docstring cannot trip it."""
      import ast
      out = []
      for top in ast.parse(source).body:
          owner = getattr(top, "name", "<module>")
          for node in ast.walk(top):
              if ((isinstance(node, ast.Name) and node.id == "SHOWN")
                      or (isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr == "SHOWN")
                      or (isinstance(node, ast.alias) and node.name == "SHOWN")):
                  out.append((node.lineno, owner, "SHOWN"))
              elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr in _RAW_BOX_READS:
                  out.append((node.lineno, owner, node.attr))
              elif (isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr == "exec"
                    and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name) and node.value.id == "QMessageBox"):
                  out.append((node.lineno, owner, "QMessageBox.exec"))
              elif (isinstance(node, ast.Call) and len(node.args) >= 2
                    and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Name) and node.args[0].id == "QMessageBox"
                    and isinstance(node.args[1], ast.Constant) and node.args[1].value == "exec"):
                  out.append((node.lineno, owner, 'setattr(QMessageBox, "exec")'))
      return sorted(set(out))


  def test_only_the_dialog_helpers_own_tests_hold_a_raw_message_box():
      """Every other test reads what the window asked through the record, so the class behind a
      question can change with one edit to the helper. The matcher is checked on a snippet first."""
      snippet = ('from tests._fixtures import SHOWN\n'
                 'def test_x(monkeypatch):\n'
                 '    monkeypatch.setattr(QMessageBox, "exec", lambda self: 0)\n'
                 '    assert SHOWN[-1].informativeText() == ""\n'
                 'def helper():\n'
                 '    """SHOWN and informativeText() in prose are not reads."""\n'
                 '    QMessageBox.exec = None\n')
      assert [(line, what) for line, _owner, what in _direct_box_reads(snippet)] == [
          (1, "SHOWN"), (3, 'setattr(QMessageBox, "exec")'), (4, "SHOWN"), (4, "informativeText"),
          (7, "QMessageBox.exec")], _direct_box_reads(snippet)
      files = sorted(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.glob("test_*.py"))
      assert len(files) >= 20, f"the scan walked only {len(files)} test files"
      found = [f"{p.name}:{line} {owner}: {what}" for p in files
               for line, owner, what in _direct_box_reads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
               if owner not in _MAY_HOLD_A_RAW_BOX]
      assert not found, (f"{len(found)} direct read(s) of a message box in "
                         f"{len({f.split(':')[0] for f in found})} file(s); read it through asked(), "
                         "all_asked(), forget_asked() and choose() (tests/_dialogs.py):\n  "
                         + "\n  ".join(found))
  ```

- [ ] **Step 2: The whole-program test, rewritten first.** Replace the body and docstring of `test_build_app_starts_and_sets_the_window_icon` (signature unchanged):
  ```python
  def test_build_app_starts_and_sets_the_window_icon(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
      """``core.gui.app.build_app`` is the one place the application-level setup runs (style, font,
      appearance, figure settings, icon, error hook); a test that builds the window itself runs none
      of it. An exception in any of that would ship with every panel test green and the program
      refusing to start.

      The icon is asserted because it fails in silence: a null QIcon is not an error, the window
      just shows Qt's default mark. build_app also makes the folder PRISM_ARTIFACTS names and
      installs it as the process's store, so the variable points at a temporary folder first.

      The second half is what the process holds afterwards. The whole program sets its look on the
      one application every later test shares, and replaces the error hook, the root log handler and
      the default store. ``whole_program`` puts each back; the comparison at the end is the proof,
      and it names every value that is not as it was found."""
      from core import logging_root
      from core.artifacts import default_store
      from tests._fixtures import process_state, whole_program
      ours = qt_app()
      monkeypatch.setenv("PRISM_ARTIFACTS", str(tmp_path / "Artifacts"))
      found = process_state(ours)
      with whole_program() as (app, window):
          assert app is ours, "the whole program must use the one application of the process"
          icon = app.windowIcon()
          assert not icon.isNull(), "build_app left the application with no window icon"
          assert {16, 32, 256} <= {s.width() for s in icon.availableSizes()}
          assert window.windowTitle() == "PRISM", window.windowTitle()
          assert default_store().root == tmp_path / "Artifacts"
          assert (tmp_path / "Artifacts").is_dir()
          assert logging_root.installed() is True, \
              "build_app must install THE root-logger handler at start-up"
          during = process_state(app)
  ```

  ```python
  @contextmanager
  def whole_program():
      """The whole program, built by ``core.gui.app.build_app`` and handed over as ``(app, window)``;
      on the way out, everything build_app set on the process is as it was found (``process_state``
      lists it). The one application serves every later test, so a test that builds the whole
      program does it through here. PRISM_ARTIFACTS must name a temporary folder first: build_app
      makes the folder it names and installs it as the process's store."""
      import sys
      import matplotlib
      from PySide6.QtCore import QCoreApplication, QEvent, Qt
      from PySide6.QtGui import QFont, QPalette
      from core import config, logging_root
      from core.artifacts import default_store, set_default_store
      from core.gui import app as gui_app
      from core.gui import theming
      if not os.environ.get("PRISM_ARTIFACTS"):
          raise AssertionError("whole_program() needs PRISM_ARTIFACTS set to a temporary folder: "
                               "build_app makes the folder it names and installs it as the process's "
                               "store, and with the variable unset that is the real Artifacts")
      app = qt_app()
      found = {"style": app.style().objectName(),       # read now: under a sheet it reads empty
               "sheet": app.styleSheet(), "palette": QPalette(app.palette()),
               "font": QFont(app.font()), "icon": app.windowIcon(),
               "names": (app.organizationName(), app.applicationName()),
               "appearance": theming.active_appearance(), "hook": sys.excepthook,
               "quiet": config.QUIET_SEGMENT_BAR, "handler": logging_root.installed(),
               "store": default_store()}
      with matplotlib.rc_context():                     # the figure settings, exactly as found
          try:
              yield gui_app.build_app([])
          finally:
              sys.excepthook = found["hook"]            # first: a slip below must not open a box
              # Then the three that cannot fail, so that a slip in the toolkit's lines below cannot
              # leave a temporary folder as the process's store or a handler on the root logger.
              set_default_store(found["store"])
              if not found["handler"]:
                  logging_root.remove()
              config.QUIET_SEGMENT_BAR = found["quiet"]
              made = theming.active_appearance()
              theming._ACTIVE = found["appearance"]
              if made is not None and made is not found["appearance"]:
                  # Gone before the colour scheme is touched: alive, it applies the look again on
                  # the next change of scheme. Its own deferred delete only, never every receiver's.
                  made.deleteLater()
                  QCoreApplication.sendPostedEvents(made, QEvent.DeferredDelete)
              app.styleHints().setColorScheme(Qt.ColorScheme.Unknown)
              app.setStyleSheet(found["sheet"])
              if found["style"]:
                  app.setStyle(found["style"])
              app.setPalette(found["palette"])
              app.setFont(found["font"])
              app.setWindowIcon(found["icon"])
              app.setOrganizationName(found["names"][0])
              app.setApplicationName(found["names"][1])
  ```

  ```python
      """The suites reach a window, a part, the inference screen and a bare run host through four
      plain functions of tests/_fixtures.py, so a constructor's arguments are written once. Three
      things make them safe under tests that build twice to stand for a relaunch, or build after a
      patch, after a settings write or inside ``use_store``: each call builds anew, at the moment of
      the call; the helpers keep nothing they built; and the inference builder does what it is handed

      plain = build_inference()
      by_the_constructor = len(refreshed)
      assert type(plain) is InferenceScreen and by_the_constructor >= 1
      session = SbiSession(cfg=object(), inf_prior=object())
      held = build_inference(session=session)
      assert held.session is session and held is not plain
      assert len(refreshed) == 2 * by_the_constructor, "the builder refreshed the gates itself"
      monkeypatch.setattr(InferenceScreen, "install_config",
                          lambda self, cfg: installed.append((self, cfg)))
      cfg = object()
      built = build_inference(cfg=cfg)
      assert installed == [(built, cfg)]

      host, other = build_run_host(), build_run_host()
      assert isinstance(host, BasePanel) and type(host) is not BasePanel and host is not other
      assert host.layout_key() == other.layout_key() == "P", "two hosts must share one layout name"
      assert type(build_run_host(BasePanel)) is BasePanel

      assert type(window) is MainWindow and type(again) is MainWindow and window is not again

      for widget in (first, second, step, plain, held, built, host, other, window, again):
          assert kept(widget) == [], f"tests/_fixtures.py keeps what it built: {kept(widget)}"


  def test_no_suite_builds_a_window_a_part_or_a_step_by_hand():
      """Every window, part, step and bare run host a suite needs comes from the builders of
      tests/_fixtures.py. Parsed, not searched: a class named in prose, or handed to a builder, is not
      a construction. Refused in every file of this folder but that one: a call of a window class
      (also through an expression that names one, as a lookup in a dict of classes), a local subclass
      of BasePanel, and a call of build_app, which whole_program alone makes. A class called through
      a variable is not seen here; the builders take the class as an argument, so no suite has a
      reason to hold one and call it."""
      import ast
      built = {"MainWindow", "InferenceScreen", "FdtPanel", "CrossValPanel", "SimulatePanel",
               "ReductionPanel", "ModelBuilderScreen", "ArtifactScreen", "ConfigPanel", "PriorPanel",
               "PosteriorPanel", "ValidatePanel", "InferPanel", "TSNPEPanel", "BasePanel"}

      def named(node):
          return ({n.id for n in ast.walk(node) if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
                  | {n.attr for n in ast.walk(node) if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute)})

      def last_name(node):
          return (node.id if isinstance(node, ast.Name)
                  else node.attr if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) else None)

      found = []
      for path in sorted(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.glob("*.py")):
          if path.name == "_fixtures.py":
              continue
          for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
              if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                  callee = last_name(node.func)
                  by_hand = (callee in built or callee == "build_app"
                             or (callee is None and bool(named(node.func) & built)))
              else:
                  by_hand = (isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef)
                             and any(last_name(base) == "BasePanel" for base in node.bases))
              if by_hand:
                  found.append(f"{path.name}:{node.lineno}")
      assert found == [], f"{len(found)} constructions written by hand: {found}"
  ```

  ```python
  def test_browse_asks_for_a_file_to_open_with_the_fields_own_filter(monkeypatch):
      """The "Browse…" button of a path field asks for a file to OPEN, titled "Select file", with no
      start value and the field's own filter. A cancelled chooser leaves the box as it was; a chosen
      path replaces its text. Reached once through the button and once directly."""
      from PySide6.QtCore import QCoreApplication, QEvent
      from PySide6.QtWidgets import QFileDialog, QPushButton
      from core.gui.widgets.labeled_inputs import PathField

      qt_app()
      calls, answers = [], iter(["", "C:/data/trace.npy"])
      monkeypatch.setattr(QFileDialog, "getOpenFileName",
                          lambda *a, **k: calls.append(("open", a, k)) or (next(answers), ""))
      monkeypatch.setattr(QFileDialog, "getSaveFileName",
                          lambda *a, **k: calls.append(("save", a, k)) or ("", ""))
      field = PathField()
      field.edit.setText("kept.csv")
      field.findChild(QPushButton).click()
      assert field.value() == "kept.csv", "a cancelled chooser changed the box"
      own = PathField("Traces (*.npy)")

      for built in (field, own):      # a field's own slot names the field, so its last name going
          built.deleteLater()         # does not delete it: its own deferred delete is delivered here
  ```

  ```python
  _CHOOSER_MODULE = "core/gui/file_chooser.py"


  def _file_dialog_uses(tree) -> list:
      """``(lineno, spelling)`` for every place a parsed module names Qt's file dialog class: an
      import of it under any alias, an attribute read off it however the class was reached
      (``QFileDialog.getSaveFileName``, ``QtWidgets.QFileDialog.getOpenFileName``), and any other use
      of the bare class (an instance built, the class handed on). A string or a comment that
      mentions it is not one."""
      out, read_through = [], set()
      for node in ast.walk(tree):
          if isinstance(node, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):
              out += [(node.lineno, "import QFileDialog") for alias in node.names
                      if alias.name.split(".")[-1] == "QFileDialog"]
          elif isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
              owner = node.value
              name = owner.attr if isinstance(owner, ast.Attribute) else getattr(owner, "id", None)
              if name == "QFileDialog":
                  out.append((node.lineno, f"QFileDialog.{node.attr}"))
                  read_through.add(id(owner))
      for node in ast.walk(tree):
          if (isinstance(node, (ast.Name, ast.Attribute)) and id(node) not in read_through
                  and (node.attr if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) else node.id) == "QFileDialog"):
              out.append((node.lineno, "QFileDialog"))
      return sorted(out)


  def test_only_the_one_chooser_module_names_the_file_dialog_class():
      """Every file chooser PRISM's own code opens goes through ONE function,
      ``core.gui.file_chooser.choose_file``, so that one guard can answer all of them.

      The suites replace two static calls for the whole session, ``QFileDialog.getSaveFileName`` and
      ``QFileDialog.getOpenFileName``. Nothing else of the class is replaced: an instance's ``exec``
      and every other static would open a real dialog, which offscreen STALLS the run instead of
      failing it. So (1) outside the one module nothing under the code roots names the class at
      all, by import, static or instance; and (2) inside it the class is imported once and each of
      the two answered statics is read exactly once, in the body of ``choose_file``. A static bound
      to a name when the module is imported would go on calling whatever stood on the class at that
      moment: the real dialog if the module is imported before the guard is installed, otherwise
      the guard's own function or one test's stand-in, which no later test could then replace. The
      scan reads the code this repository holds: the toolbar matplotlib gives a popped-out figure
      opens a save chooser from matplotlib's own code, which no scan here sees, and the guard
      answers that one because it stands on the static itself.

      The scanner is checked on a SNIPPET first, so the walk cannot pass by finding nothing."""
      from tests._fixtures import CODE_FILES, CODE_ROOTS
      snippet = ast.parse(
          'from PySide6.QtWidgets import QFileDialog\n'                      # 1: the import itself
          'from PySide6.QtWidgets import QFileDialog as Chooser\n'           # 2: under another name
          'path, _ = QFileDialog.getSaveFileName(self, "t", "", "f")\n'     # 3: an answered static
          'path, _ = QtWidgets.QFileDialog.getOpenFileName(self, "t")\n'    # 4: through the module
          'folder = QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory(self, "t")\n'          # 5: a static nobody answers
          'dialog = QFileDialog(self)\n'                                     # 6: an instance
          'dialog.exec()\n'
          'path = choose_file(self, "t", "", "f", save=True)\n'             # what is wanted
          'note = "QFileDialog.getSaveFileName in a string is no call"\n')
      assert _file_dialog_uses(snippet) == [
          (1, "import QFileDialog"), (2, "import QFileDialog"), (3, "QFileDialog.getSaveFileName"),
          (4, "QFileDialog.getOpenFileName"), (5, "QFileDialog.getExistingDirectory"),
          (6, "QFileDialog")], _file_dialog_uses(snippet)

      files = [py for sub in CODE_ROOTS for py in sorted((REPO / sub).rglob("*.py"))]
      files += [REPO / name for name in CODE_FILES]
      assert len(files) >= 20, f"the scan walked only {len(files)} files -- CODE_ROOTS is {CODE_ROOTS}"
      found = []
      for py in files:
          rel = py.relative_to(REPO).as_posix()
          if rel == _CHOOSER_MODULE:
              continue
          for ln, spelling in _file_dialog_uses(ast.parse(py.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
              found.append(f"{rel}:{ln}: {spelling}")
      assert not found, ("Qt's file dialog is named outside " + _CHOOSER_MODULE + ". The suites answer "
                         "the two chooser calls that module makes and nothing else, so any other "
                         "chooser opens for real and stalls the run. Call "
                         "core.gui.file_chooser.choose_file instead:\n" + "\n".join(found))
      chooser = ast.parse((REPO / _CHOOSER_MODULE).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
      fn = next(n for n in chooser.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "choose_file")
      in_body = sorted(s for stmt in fn.body for _ln, s in _file_dialog_uses(stmt))
      assert in_body == ["QFileDialog.getOpenFileName", "QFileDialog.getSaveFileName"], in_body
      everywhere = sorted(s for _ln, s in _file_dialog_uses(chooser))
      assert everywhere == in_body + ["import QFileDialog"], everywhere


  def test_the_chooser_module_costs_only_the_toolkit():
      """Two torch-free widget modules call the chooser (the typed input fields and the pop-out
      figure windows), so the module they import must cost the toolkit and nothing else: its import
      statements name ``PySide6.QtWidgets`` alone, and a fresh interpreter that imports it holds
      neither torch nor any module of PRISM's that reaches torch. The subprocess is the real pin: in
      this process torch is long since imported."""

      probe = ("import sys; import core.gui.file_chooser; "
               "heavy = ('core.config', 'core.gui.fields', 'core.registry', 'core.Helpers.file_manager'); "
               "bad = sorted(m for m in sys.modules if m == 'torch' or m.startswith('torch.') or m in heavy); "
               "sys.exit(repr(bad) if bad else 0)")
      r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", probe], cwd=str(REPO), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
      assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr
  ```

  ```python
  """The one place PRISM's own code opens a file chooser.

  Every "Save…", "Save As…" and "Browse…" button calls ``choose_file``. It hands the system's dialog
  the title, the start value and the filter exactly as given and returns the path, or "" when the
  dialog was cancelled. It adds no extension, remembers no folder and stores nothing: what is done
  with the path is the caller's.

  The two static calls are looked up on the class EACH TIME the function runs, never bound to a name
  when this module is imported. The suites replace both for the whole session, because a chooser
  nobody answers would otherwise open for real and stall the run; a name bound at import would go on
  calling whatever stood on the class at that moment.

  One chooser does not come through here: the toolbar matplotlib gives a popped-out figure opens its
  own, from matplotlib's code.
  """
  from PySide6.QtWidgets import QFileDialog


  def choose_file(parent, title: str, start: str = "", filter: str = "", *, save: bool) -> str:
      """Ask for a file to save to (``save=True``) or to open (``save=False``).

      ``parent`` is the widget the dialog belongs to, or None. ``start`` is empty or a suggested file
      name; ``filter`` is in Qt's own form, entries joined by ``;;``. Returns the chosen path, or ""
      when the dialog was cancelled."""
      ask = QFileDialog.getSaveFileName if save else QFileDialog.getOpenFileName
      path, _chosen_filter = ask(parent, title, start, filter)
      return path
  ```

  ```python
  def test_the_record_of_a_figure_holds_everything_but_its_colours():
      """The record the next test compares must see a changed number, width, dash, marker, transparency
      or label, and must not see a changed colour; and two builds of one figure must give one record."""
      import numpy as np
      from matplotlib.figure import Figure

      def build(colour="steelblue", width=1.0, dash="--", alpha=0.25, label="band", lift=0.0, marker="o"):
          t = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 8)
          ax = Figure().add_subplot()
          ax.fill_between(t, t - 0.1, t + 0.1, alpha=alpha, color=colour, label=label)
          ax.plot(t, t + lift, color=colour, linewidth=width, linestyle=dash)
          ax.plot(t, 1.0 - t, marker=marker, linestyle="none", color=colour)
          ax.scatter(t[:2], t[:2], c=colour, s=40)
          ax.axvspan(0.2, 0.4, color=colour, alpha=0.1)
          ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "note", color=colour)
          return _digest(_drawn(ax.figure))

      same = build()
      assert build() == same, "two builds of one figure differ: the record is not repeatable"
      assert build(colour="#0072B2") == same, "a colour reached the record"
      for change in (dict(width=1.1), dict(dash="-."), dict(alpha=0.3), dict(label="Band"),
                     dict(lift=1e-6), dict(marker=".")):
          assert build(**change) != same, f"the record does not see {change}"
  ```

  ```python
  # ── what a figure draws, its colours left out ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  def _plain(value):
      """Anything an artist hands back, as text and rounded numbers that compare equal run after run.
      Ten significant digits, so the last bits of a float never decide a comparison."""
      import numpy as np
      if value is None or isinstance(value, (str, bool)):
          return value
      if isinstance(value, (int, float, np.integer, np.floating)):
          v = float(value)
          return repr(v) if (v != v or v in (float("inf"), float("-inf"))) else float(f"{v:.10g}")
      if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
          flat = np.ma.filled(np.ma.asarray(value, dtype=float), np.nan)
          return {"shape": list(flat.shape), "values": [_plain(v) for v in flat.ravel()]}
      if isinstance(value, dict):
          return {str(k): _plain(v) for k, v in value.items()}
      if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
          return [_plain(v) for v in value]
      return str(value)

  def _drawn(fig) -> dict:
      """What a figure draws, as plain data: every number, width, dash, marker, transparency, label,
      drawing order and colour-map name of every artist on every axes, and NO colour. Read off the
      artists, never off pixels, so the page and the lettering do not enter it."""
      import numpy as np

      def common(a):
          solid = hasattr(a, "do_3d_projection")      # a 3-D artist's drawing order is set when it is drawn
          return {"kind": type(a).__name__, "label": a.get_label(), "alpha": a.get_alpha(),
                  "order": None if solid else a.get_zorder(),
                  "effects": [type(e).__name__ for e in (a.get_path_effects() or [])]}

      def line(ln):
          data = ln.get_data_3d() if hasattr(ln, "get_data_3d") else ln.get_data(orig=False)
          return dict(common(ln), data=[np.asarray(d, dtype=float) for d in data], style=ln.get_linestyle(),
                      width=ln.get_linewidth(), marker=str(ln.get_marker()), marker_size=ln.get_markersize(),
                      steps=ln.get_drawstyle())

      def collection(c):
          out = dict(common(c), widths=np.asarray(c.get_linewidths(), dtype=float), styles=c.get_linestyles())
          if hasattr(c, "get_coordinates"):                       # a colour mesh: its corners
              out["mesh"] = np.asarray(c.get_coordinates())
          elif not hasattr(c, "do_3d_projection"):                # a 3-D artist's paths are its projection
              out["offsets"] = np.asarray(c.get_offsets())
              out["paths"] = [np.asarray(p.vertices) for p in c.get_paths()]
          if hasattr(c, "get_sizes"):
              out["sizes"] = np.asarray(c.get_sizes(), dtype=float)
          if c.get_array() is not None:
              out.update(values=np.asarray(c.get_array()), limits=c.get_clim(), colour_map=c.get_cmap().name)
          return out

      def patch(p):
          where = p.get_bbox().bounds if hasattr(p, "get_bbox") else np.asarray(p.get_path().vertices)
          return dict(common(p), where=where, width=p.get_linewidth(), style=p.get_linestyle(), hatch=p.get_hatch())

      def text(t):
          box = t.get_bbox_patch()
          return dict(common(t), text=t.get_text(), at=t.get_position(), size=t.get_fontsize(),
                      face=t.get_fontfamily(), align=[t.get_ha(), t.get_va()],
                      box=None if box is None else [type(box.get_boxstyle()).__name__, box.get_alpha()])

      def image(im):
          return dict(common(im), values=np.asarray(im.get_array()), limits=im.get_clim(),
                      colour_map=im.get_cmap().name, extent=im.get_extent())

      def axes(ax):
          legend = ax.get_legend()
          out = {"title": ax.get_title(), "x": [ax.get_xlabel(), ax.get_xscale(), ax.get_xlim()],
                 "y": [ax.get_ylabel(), ax.get_yscale(), ax.get_ylim()],
                 "lines": [line(a) for a in ax.lines], "collections": [collection(a) for a in ax.collections],
                 "patches": [patch(a) for a in ax.patches], "texts": [text(a) for a in ax.texts],
                 "images": [image(a) for a in ax.images],
                 "tables": [{f"{r},{c}": cell.get_text().get_text() for (r, c), cell in sorted(t.get_celld().items())}
                            for t in ax.tables],
                 "legend": None if legend is None else [t.get_text() for t in legend.get_texts()]}
          if hasattr(ax, "get_zlim"):
              out["z"] = [ax.get_zlabel(), ax.get_zlim()]
          return out

      return _plain({"size": fig.get_size_inches(), "heading": fig.get_suptitle(),
                     "axes": [axes(ax) for ax in fig.axes]})

  def _digest(record) -> str:
      import hashlib
      import json
      return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
  ```

The tables hold the numbers of Windows' ordinary text size; a READER passes a length through `scaled()` (4.8's own words are "is scaled before the first widget": every later task of the stage is written to the reader's call). The keys below are weights and radii: a reader takes them as they are, and `UNSCALED` names them as `"TABLE.key"`.

  | not scaled | by |
  |---|---|
  | `SIZE.rule`, `SIZE.hair`, `SIZE.bar`, `SIZE.radius`, `SIZE.hatch_step`, `SIZE.focus_ring`, `SIZE.focus_gap`; `AXIS.mark_w`, `AXIS.mark_halo`; `FIGURE.axis_w`, `FIGURE.line_w` | 4.8's own list |

  | `SIZE.scroll_bar`, `SIZE.scroll_gap`, `SIZE.scroll_handle` (all three of its numbers) | 4.8 names the scroll bar; departure 17: its gap and its handle go with it, so no key is half scaled |

Everything else in the six tables is a length and is scaled by its reader, the 18 px indicator, the 16 and 24 px markers, the hatch key, `FIGURE.best_mark` and `STEP.line_x` among them; so are a `TYPE` row's size and line height. - **Numbers and dates: what 4.3 does not say (ruled to stand as written here).** `number_text`: a whole number (`numbers.Integral`, so numpy's too) is `format(int(value), ",")`; any other real number is `format(float(value), ",")`, Python's shortest form that reads back the same, with commas in its whole part ("2,048.0", "0.05"); the minus is the keyboard's hyphen, so the text reads back in a field; a `bool`, a `str`, `None` or anything else raises `TypeError` (test for `bool` FIRST: Python counts `True` among the whole numbers); a unit is the caller's (`number_text(40.1) + " %"`); an identifier (a seed, a record's id) is not a quantity and is never handed to it (4.3), which its docstring says. `date_text`: "3 Oct 2026, 14:02" is the day with no leading zero, the month's three letters, the year, a comma, then hours and minutes on the 24-hour clock, two digits each, seconds dropped. With `now` handed in and `abs(when - now) < timedelta(days=7)`, ahead of now as well as behind it (an expected end is ahead), it is "Sun 4 Oct, 12:10": the weekday's three letters and no year; exactly seven days is outside. Nothing is converted between zones: the fields of `when` are written as handed in, and a pair of which one has a zone and the other none raises Python's own `TypeError`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `tests/test_look.py`, whole, and see every test fail.** The block below is the file (two blank lines between top-level definitions in the file; the block prints one). The block stands two spaces in, as every block of this list does: take exactly two spaces off the front of EVERY line, the lines inside the long string `_FRESH` among them (that string is handed to a child interpreter as a program, so its lines must begin in the first column). This block is the only source: the folder `t6_proto` beside the record script holds an earlier trial of it (the fixed-width faces in another order, one test and a few assertions fewer) and is not to be copied from.

  ```python
  """The look: its one table of colours, type and sizes, and the functions every reader of it shares.

  Nothing here imports torch, so the look can be tested without the engine;
  ``test_the_look_and_this_file_load_without_the_engine`` proves it in a fresh interpreter, which runs this whole file:
  its module level holds imports, constants and definitions only. One application object serves every suite of a run,
  so the theme and the text factor are changed here only inside a helper or a fixture that puts back what it found:
  ``theme`` and ``text_size`` are the two helpers for it.
  """
  import ast
  import contextlib
  import datetime
  import hashlib
  import json
  import subprocess
  import sys
  import types
  from pathlib import Path

  import pytest

  from core.gui import design

  REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
  # every module of the look that exists; a new one joins this tuple in the commit that adds it, and the
  # fresh-interpreter test is then its proof that it loads no engine
  LOOK_MODULES = ("core.gui.design", "core.gui.fonts", "core.gui.theming", "core.gui.mpl_theme", "core.gui.settings",
                  "core.gui.file_chooser", "core.gui.widgets.labeled_inputs")
  # what the look may never load: the engine, and the modules that reach it
  FORBIDDEN_MODULES = ("torch", "core.config", "core.registry", "core.gui.fields", "core.Helpers.file_manager", "tests._fixtures")

  @contextlib.contextmanager
  def theme(dark):
      """The theme in force inside the block; what was in force before is put back."""
      was = design.is_dark()
      design.set_dark(dark)
      try:
          yield
      finally:
          design.set_dark(was)

  @contextlib.contextmanager
  def text_size(factor):
      """The text factor in force inside the block; what was in force before is put back."""
      was = design.text_scale()
      design.set_text_scale(factor)
      try:
          yield
      finally:
          design.set_text_scale(was)

  # name: (light, dark). Typed a second time on purpose, so that a changed colour fails here by name.
  EXPECTED_COLOURS = {
  ```
