  ```python
  @contextlib.contextmanager
  def _figure_settings_kept():
      """matplotlib's process-wide settings may be written inside the block; what was in force before
      is put back."""
      import matplotlib
      saved = dict(matplotlib.rcParams)
      try:
          yield
      finally:
          matplotlib.rcParams.update(saved)

  _LIGHT_FIGURE_SETTINGS = {
      "figure.facecolor": "#FFFFFF", "figure.edgecolor": "#FFFFFF",
      "savefig.facecolor": "#FFFFFF", "savefig.edgecolor": "#FFFFFF",
      "axes.facecolor": "#FFFFFF", "axes.edgecolor": "#1A1A1A",
      "axes.labelcolor": "#1A1A1A", "axes.titlecolor": "#1A1A1A", "text.color": "#1A1A1A",
      "xtick.color": "#1A1A1A", "ytick.color": "#1A1A1A",
      "xtick.labelcolor": "#4D4D4D", "ytick.labelcolor": "#4D4D4D", "grid.color": "#D4D4D4",
      "legend.facecolor": "#FFFFFF", "legend.edgecolor": "#FFFFFF", "legend.framealpha": 1.0,
      "axes.spines.top": False, "axes.spines.right": False,
      "xtick.direction": "out", "ytick.direction": "out",
      "xtick.major.size": 3.6, "ytick.major.size": 3.6,
      "axes.linewidth": 0.72, "xtick.major.width": 0.72, "ytick.major.width": 0.72,
      "lines.linewidth": 1.44, "lines.solid_joinstyle": "round", "lines.dash_joinstyle": "round",
      "axes.unicode_minus": True, "font.family": ["Inter", "DejaVu Sans"],
  }
  _LINE_COLOURS = ["#1A1A1A", "#0072B2", "#C24E00", "#007A5A", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#CC79A7"]

  def test_the_figure_settings_are_the_light_column_and_nothing_else():
      from core.gui import mpl_theme
      rc = mpl_theme._rc()
      cycle = rc.pop("axes.prop_cycle")
      assert set(rc) == set(_LIGHT_FIGURE_SETTINGS), sorted(set(rc) ^ set(_LIGHT_FIGURE_SETTINGS))
      for name, value in _LIGHT_FIGURE_SETTINGS.items():
          assert rc[name] == (pytest.approx(value) if isinstance(value, float) else value), name
      assert cycle.keys == {"color"}, "the cycle carries more than a colour"
      assert cycle.by_key()["color"] == _LINE_COLOURS
      assert _LINE_COLOURS == [design.hex_colour(name, dark=False) for name in design.SERIES]

  def test_the_figure_settings_do_not_follow_the_theme_or_the_text_size():
      """Neither way a theme reaches the window moves a figure setting: not the look's own flag
      (nor the text factor beside it), and not the signal a change of appearance sends."""
      import matplotlib
      from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, Signal
      from core.gui import mpl_theme

      class DarkAppearance(QObject):            # all that install() may ask of an appearance
          theme_changed = Signal(bool)

          def is_dark(self):
              return True

      with theme(False), text_size(1.0):
          light = mpl_theme._rc()
      with theme(True), text_size(2.0), _figure_settings_kept():
          assert mpl_theme._rc() == light
          appearance = DarkAppearance()
          mpl_theme.install(appearance)
          assert {name: matplotlib.rcParams[name] for name in light} == light, \
              "under a dark appearance the settings written are not the light ones"
          matplotlib.rcParams["figure.facecolor"] = "#123456"      # a mark no setting of the look has
          appearance.theme_changed.emit(False)
          appearance.theme_changed.emit(True)
          assert matplotlib.rcParams["figure.facecolor"] == "#123456", \
              "a change of theme rewrote the figure settings"

  def test_the_figure_settings_name_inter_only_when_both_files_reached_matplotlib(monkeypatch):
      from core.gui import fonts, mpl_theme
      monkeypatch.setattr(fonts, "register_with_matplotlib", lambda: False)
      assert "font.family" not in mpl_theme._rc() and len(mpl_theme._rc()) == 31
      monkeypatch.setattr(fonts, "register_with_matplotlib", lambda: True)
      assert mpl_theme._rc()["font.family"] == ["Inter", "DejaVu Sans"]

  def test_under_the_figure_settings_unnamed_lines_take_the_seven_colours_in_order():
      from matplotlib.figure import Figure
      from core.gui import mpl_theme
      with _figure_settings_kept():
          mpl_theme.apply_mpl_theme()
          ax = Figure().add_subplot()
          lines = [ax.plot([0, 1], [i, i + 1])[0] for i in range(8)]
          assert [ln.get_color() for ln in lines] == _LINE_COLOURS + _LINE_COLOURS[:1]
          assert {ln.get_linestyle() for ln in lines} == {"-"}
          assert not ax.spines["top"].get_visible() and not ax.spines["right"].get_visible()

  def test_under_the_figure_settings_a_character_the_lettering_lacks_is_drawn_without_a_warning():
      """A record's or a parameter's name can hold a character Inter has no drawing for. The settings
      name a second face for those, so the label is drawn and matplotlib warns of no missing glyph.
      With Inter alone the same label does warn, which is what makes this test able to fail."""
      import io
      import warnings
      import matplotlib
      from matplotlib.figure import Figure
      from core.gui import mpl_theme

      def missing_glyphs():
          fig = Figure()
          ax = fig.add_subplot()
          ax.set_title("run \u2716 seven")              # a heavy multiplication sign: not in Inter
          ax.set_xlabel("ordinary words")
          with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
              warnings.simplefilter("always")
              fig.savefig(io.BytesIO(), format="png")
          return [str(w.message) for w in caught if "missing from font" in str(w.message)]

      with _figure_settings_kept():
          mpl_theme.apply_mpl_theme()
          assert matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"][0] == "Inter", "Inter did not reach matplotlib"
          assert missing_glyphs() == []
          matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = ["Inter"]
          assert missing_glyphs(), "this label no longer holds a character Inter lacks: choose another"
  ```

  ```python
  """matplotlib's process-wide settings for every figure the engine builds.

  They are the LIGHT side of the look's table in both appearances, written once, when the application
  is built; a change of appearance does not touch them. So a stored figure never carries dark colours,
  and a run that straddles a change of appearance cannot build a figure under one set of settings and
  save it under another. The lengths do not grow with the text size: a stored figure must not depend
  on the computer that drew it.

  The engine's plotting code imports nothing of the window. It reads matplotlib's settings, which are
  these in the window and matplotlib's own on the command line. A figure already on screen is a
  picture and is not drawn again.
  """
  # _rc:
  """The figure settings, built anew at each call: the light side of the look's table whatever the
  theme in force, the three lengths as the table holds them, the lettering face only when matplotlib
  has both of its files."""
  # apply_mpl_theme:
  """Write the light figure settings into matplotlib's process-wide settings. Only a figure built
  after the call takes them."""
  # install:
  """Write the light figure settings now. Nothing without an appearance; and it listens to nothing,
  so a later change of appearance leaves the settings as they are."""
  ```

Then append at the end of the file the block below (it stands two spaces in, as every block of this list does: take exactly two spaces off the front of every line):
  ```python
  # ── the plotting code's line colours ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  _PLOTTING_FILES = ("core/Helpers/visualizers.py", "core/FDT/plots.py", "core/FDT/compare.py",
                     "core/FDT/cross_validation_plots.py", "core/Reduction/plots.py",
                     "core/diagnostics/identifiability.py", "core/diagnostics/probes.py")
  _OLD_LINE_COLOURS = frozenset({"steelblue", "tab:blue", "red", "r", "crimson", "tab:red", "green",
                                 "tab:green", "darkorange", "orange", "tab:orange", "gray"})
  _COLOUR_KEYWORDS = frozenset({"color", "c", "colors", "edgecolor", "edgecolors", "facecolor",
                                "facecolors", "ecolor", "markerfacecolor", "markeredgecolor", "mfc",
                                "mec", "fc", "ec", "foreground", "labelcolor"})
  _LINE_CALLS = frozenset({"plot", "semilogx", "semilogy", "loglog", "errorbar", "step", "stem"})
  _LINE_FORMAT = re.compile(r"(?:[bgrcmykw]|--|-\.|[-:.,ov^<>1-4sp*hH+xXDd|_])+")


  def _own_colour_arguments(tree) -> list:
      """``(line, text)`` for every colour a call names itself: one of the old colour names, a hex
      value or a ``tab:`` name as a colour keyword's value, and a line format string that carries a
      colour letter other than white or black. Parsed, so a colour name in a comment, a label or a
      file mode is not an argument."""
      hits = []
      for node in ast.walk(tree):
          if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
              continue
          for kw in node.keywords:
              if kw.arg in _COLOUR_KEYWORDS:
                  hits += [(c.lineno, c.value) for c in ast.walk(kw.value)
                           if isinstance(c, ast.Constant) and isinstance(c.value, str)
                           and (c.value in _OLD_LINE_COLOURS or c.value.startswith(("#", "tab:")))]
          if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute) and node.func.attr in _LINE_CALLS:
              formats = [a for a in node.args if isinstance(a, ast.Constant) and isinstance(a.value, str)]
              formats += [kw.value for kw in node.keywords if kw.arg == "fmt"
                          and isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant) and isinstance(kw.value.value, str)]
              hits += [(a.lineno, a.value) for a in formats
                       if _LINE_FORMAT.fullmatch(a.value) and set(a.value) & set("bgrcmy")]
      return sorted(hits)


  def test_the_plotting_colour_scan_catches_each_form_and_spares_what_stays():
      """The scanner is checked on snippets first: with the tree clean, the walk of the seven files
      would go on passing if the scanner stopped matching anything."""
      caught = ast.parse("ax.plot(x, y, color='steelblue')\n"
                         "ax.scatter(x, y, c='gray', edgecolors='none')\n"
                         "ax.axhline(0.0, color='r')\n"
                         "ax.plot(x, y, 'r--')\n"
                         "ax.errorbar(x, y, fmt='go')\n"
                         "ax.bar(x, y, color=['tab:blue', 'tab:red'])\n"
                         "ax.axvline(1.0, color='#0072B2')\n")
      assert _own_colour_arguments(caught) == [
          (1, "steelblue"), (2, "gray"), (3, "r"), (4, "r--"), (5, "go"), (6, "tab:blue"),
          (6, "tab:red"), (7, "#0072B2")]
      spared = ast.parse("ax.plot(x, y, 'o-', color=plot_colours.BLUE)\n"
                         "ax.plot(x, y, 'w-', lw=2)\n"
                         "ax.text(0, 0, 'r', color='white' if dark else 'black')\n"
                         "ax.axhline(0, color=plt.rcParams['axes.edgecolor'])\n"
                         "ax.scatter(x, y, c=plot_colours.ORANGE, edgecolors='none')\n"
                         "ax.imshow(data, cmap='viridis')\n"
                         "ax.plot(x, y, label='red')\n"
                         "open(path, 'r')\n")
      assert _own_colour_arguments(spared) == []


  def test_no_plotting_file_names_a_line_colour_of_its_own():
      """The seven plotting files take every named colour from core/Helpers/plot_colours.py, so a
      figure saved from the command line and one saved from the window carry the same ones. White
      and black lettering, the white line over a colour map, a colour read from matplotlib's
      settings and a colour map stay; a line that names no colour takes matplotlib's cycle."""
      left = []
      for rel in _PLOTTING_FILES:
          tree = ast.parse((REPO / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
          left += [f"{rel}:{line} {text!r}" for line, text in _own_colour_arguments(tree)]
      assert left == [], (f"{len(left)} colour argument(s) still name a colour of their own; each "
                          f"takes its colour from core/Helpers/plot_colours.py:\n  " + "\n  ".join(left))


  def test_the_plotting_colours_module_imports_nothing_but_itself():
      """The effective-temperature and reduction plotting files, and a comparison of saved runs, must
      be able to import the colours with neither torch nor matplotlib behind them. RUN in a fresh
      interpreter: this process already holds both, so a look at its own modules would prove
      nothing. The module's own statements are read too: it holds four values and imports nothing."""
      probe = ("import sys\n"
               "before = set(sys.modules)\n"
               "import core.Helpers.plot_colours\n"
               "new = sorted(set(sys.modules) - before)\n"
               "sys.exit(0 if new == ['core', 'core.Helpers', 'core.Helpers.plot_colours'] else repr(new))\n")
      r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", probe], cwd=str(REPO), capture_output=True, text=True,
                         timeout=120)
      assert r.returncode == 0, r.stdout + r.stderr
      tree = ast.parse((REPO / "core" / "Helpers" / "plot_colours.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
      imports = [n.lineno for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom))]
      assert imports == [], f"core/Helpers/plot_colours.py imports at lines {imports}"


  def test_the_plotting_colours_are_the_second_to_fifth_line_colours():
      """The engine holds its own copy of four colours, so that it imports nothing of the window;
      this is what keeps the copy equal to the window's table. The first line colour, the ink, is
      not held (a plotting function reads it from matplotlib's settings), and nothing else is."""
      from core.Helpers import plot_colours
      held = (plot_colours.BLUE, plot_colours.VERMILION, plot_colours.GREEN, plot_colours.ORANGE)
      assert held == ("#0072B2", "#C24E00", "#007A5A", "#E69F00")
      assert design.SERIES[1:5] == ("series_2", "err", "ok", "warn")
      assert held == tuple(design.COLOURS[name][0] for name in design.SERIES[1:5])
      assert sorted(n for n in vars(plot_colours) if not n.startswith("_")) == [
          "BLUE", "GREEN", "ORANGE", "VERMILION"]
  ```

  ```python
  _ON_A_SHAPE = ("paper", "on_err", "warn_mark")      # the marks that stand on a filled shape


  def _shade(name: str, disabled: bool) -> QColor:
      """A colour of the look for one part of a marker. Drawn disabled, a shape takes the colour of
      disabled text and a mark that stands on it stays the page's colour, so a tick, a cross or a half
      never vanishes into its shape."""
      if not disabled:
          return design.colour(name)
      return design.colour("paper" if name in _ON_A_SHAPE else "disabled_ink")


  def fill_px(painter, rect: QRectF, colour: QColor, *, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0,
              left: int = 0, right: int = 0) -> None:
      """Rule the named edges of ``rect``: ``top=2`` is a rule 2 logical pixels thick along its top edge.
      A rule's thickness is a whole number of device pixels, worked out once, rounded down as a browser
      rounds a border and never under one; it is laid from the edge it is named for. So it has one weight
      wherever it falls, stays inside its rectangle, and no widget beside it covers part of it. Left to
      the painter, a 1 px line at 150 % is 1 or 2 pixels by position. No edge named, nothing painted."""
      to_device = painter.deviceTransform()
      to_logical, invertible = to_device.inverted()
      if not invertible or rect.width() <= 0 or rect.height() <= 0:
          return
      near, far = to_device.map(rect.topLeft()), to_device.map(rect.bottomRight())
      x0, x1 = math.floor(near.x() + 0.5), math.floor(far.x() + 0.5)
      y0, y1 = math.floor(near.y() + 0.5), math.floor(far.y() + 0.5)

      def whole(pixels, per_pixel):
          return max(1, math.floor(pixels * abs(per_pixel) + 1e-6))

      bands = []
      if top:
          bands.append((x0, y0, x1, y0 + whole(top, to_device.m22())))
      if bottom:
          bands.append((x0, y1 - whole(bottom, to_device.m22()), x1, y1))
      if left:
          bands.append((x0, y0, x0 + whole(left, to_device.m11()), y1))
      if right:
          bands.append((x1 - whole(right, to_device.m11()), y0, x1, y1))
      for a, b, c, d in bands:
          painter.fillRect(QRectF(to_logical.map(QPointF(a, b)), to_logical.map(QPointF(c, d))), colour)
  ```

- **`fill_px` is called in the registry's form, not the sample's.** `rect` is the box whose edges are ruled; each keyword is the weight, in logical pixels, of the rule along that edge. The sample's `fill_px(p, QRectF(0, h - 2, w, 2), c, from_bottom=True)` is `paint.fill_px(painter, QRectF(0, 0, w, h), c, bottom=2)`.

It has no accessible name: a marker always stands beside its word (4.5). `PaintedIcon.paint` calls `paint.paint_marker` (through the module, as written here: Step 6's last test replaces that name) for a square at the LEFT of `rect`, centred vertically, side `min(rect.width(), rect.height())`, with `disabled=(mode == QIcon.Disabled)`. `pixmap` fills a `QPixmap(size)` with `Qt.transparent`, holds a painter on it in a name, calls `self.paint(painter, QRect(QPoint(0, 0), size), mode, state)` inside a `try` and ends the painter in its `finally` (trap 11), then returns the pixmap. `painted_icon(kind)` returns `QIcon(PaintedIcon(kind))`. `clone` is exactly:

  ```python
  _TWINS: list = []           # every engine that clone() made, kept alive: see PaintedIcon.clone


  class PaintedIcon(QIconEngine):
      ...

      def clone(self):
          """A twin for a copy of the icon that is being changed. The twin is put in ``_TWINS`` before
          it is handed over: a new engine that no name holds is gone before the toolkit takes it, and
          the process ends without a word."""
          twin = PaintedIcon(self._kind)
          _TWINS.append(twin)
          return twin
  ```

  ```python
  # ── painted devices: markers, glyphs, icons, ruled lines, the hatching ─────────────────────────
  _SCALINGS = (1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0)                    # the display scalings a device is drawn at
  _BLANK = QColor(255, 0, 255)                         # a ground no colour of the look can be taken for
  _BARE = _BLANK.name().upper()                        # that ground, as the colour of a pixel is named
  _HEAVY_RULE = {1.0: 2, 1.25: 2, 1.5: 3, 2.0: 4}      # a 2 px rule in device pixels at each scaling
  _HAIR_RULE = {1.0: 1, 1.25: 1, 1.5: 1, 2.0: 2}       # a 1 px rule
  # Where each shape shows which colour, and where it leaves the ground bare, in the 16-unit box a
  # marker is drawn in. Every point lies on the middle of a stroke or well inside a fill.
  _MARK_SHOWS = {
      "done": ((8, 2.5, "ink"), (9.25, 8.2, "paper")), "now": ((8, 8, "accent"),),
      "later": ((14.42, 9.04, "ink_3"),), "lock": ((8, 11, "ink_2"), (8, 2, "ink_2")),
      "half": ((5, 8, "ink"), (11, 8, "paper"), (8, 1, "ink")), "none": ((8, 8, "ink_3"),),
      "fine": ((8, 1, "ok"), (9.1, 8.2, "ok")), "info": ((8, 1, "ink_2"), (8, 4.9, "ink_2"), (8, 9.6, "ink_2")),
      "warn": ((5, 12.5, "warn"), (8, 8, "warn_mark"), (8, 12.1, "warn_mark"), (8, 14.3, "warn_edge")),
      "err": ((2, 8, "err"), (8, 8, "on_err"), (5.5, 5.5, "on_err")), "stop": ((8, 8, "err"),),
      "chev_right": ((10.5, 8, "ink"),), "chev_down": ((8, 10.5, "ink"),), "chev_up": ((8, 5.5, "ink"),),
      "help": ((8, 1, "ink"), (8, 12, "ink")),
  }
  _MARK_BARE = {
      "done": ((0.5, 0.5),), "now": ((1.5, 1.5),), "later": ((8, 8), (13.78, 10.97)), "lock": ((8, 5.5),),
      "half": ((0.5, 0.5),), "none": ((8, 4),), "fine": ((10, 12),), "info": ((5, 8),), "warn": ((2, 3),),
      "err": ((0.1, 0.1),), "chev_right": ((4, 8), (12.5, 8)), "chev_down": ((8, 5.5),),
      "chev_up": ((8, 10.5),), "help": ((3.5, 8),), "stop": ((1.5, 8),),
  }
  _MARK_INNER = ("paper", "on_err", "warn_mark")       # the marks that stand ON a filled shape


  def _screen(width, height, ratio, ground=_BLANK, draw=None):
      """A picture standing in for a screen at one scaling, on a ground of one colour, with
      ``draw(painter)`` painted into it. The painter is ended whatever ``draw`` does: a picture that
      goes while a painter still paints on it ends the whole run, where the test should only fail."""
      image = _image(width, height, ratio)             # its size is rounded UP there: rounded down, a last row is cut
      image.fill(ground)
      if draw is not None:
          painter = QPainter(image)
          try:
              draw(painter)
          finally:
              painter.end()
      return image


  def _screen_of(widget, ratio, ground=_BLANK):
      """A widget painted into such a picture, with no ground of its own under it."""
      image = _screen(widget.width(), widget.height(), ratio, ground)
      widget.render(image, QPoint(0, 0), QRegion(), QWidget.RenderFlag.DrawChildren)
      return image


  def _every_pixel(image):
      return [image.pixelColor(x, y) for y in range(image.height()) for x in range(image.width())]


  def _run_of(image, colour, *, column=None, row=None):
      """Where one colour's device pixels lie down one column, or along one row."""
      if column is not None:
          return [y for y in range(image.height()) if image.pixelColor(column, y) == colour]
      return [x for x in range(image.width()) if image.pixelColor(x, row) == colour]


  def _device_edge(value):
      return int(math.floor(value + 0.5))


  def test_the_ten_states_and_the_five_glyphs_are_named_once():
      assert paint.MARKERS == ("done", "now", "later", "lock", "half", "none", "fine", "info", "warn", "err")
      assert paint.GLYPHS == ("chev_right", "chev_down", "chev_up", "help", "stop")
      assert set(_MARK_SHOWS) == set(_MARK_BARE) == set(paint.MARKERS + paint.GLYPHS)


  def test_each_marker_and_glyph_shows_its_colours_in_both_themes_at_four_scalings():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])

      def draw(painter):
          paint.paint_marker(painter, kind, QRectF(4, 4, 64, 64))                  # 4 px to a unit
          assert painter.transform().isIdentity() and not painter.testRenderHint(QPainter.Antialiasing)   # left as found

      for dark, ratio, kind in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS, paint.MARKERS + paint.GLYPHS):
          with theme(dark):
              image = _screen(72, 72, ratio, draw=draw)
              for x, y, name in _MARK_SHOWS[kind]:
                  assert _at(image, 4 + 4 * x, 4 + 4 * y) == design.hex_colour(name), (kind, dark, ratio, x, y, name)
              for x, y in _MARK_BARE[kind]:
                  assert _at(image, 4 + 4 * x, 4 + 4 * y) == _BARE, (kind, dark, ratio, x, y)


  def test_a_disabled_marker_keeps_its_inner_mark():
      """Drawn disabled, a shape takes the colour of disabled text and the mark that stands on it stays
      the page's colour: a tick, a cross or a half must not vanish into its shape."""
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      for dark, ratio, kind in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS, paint.MARKERS + paint.GLYPHS):
          with theme(dark):
              image = _screen(72, 72, ratio, draw=lambda p: paint.paint_marker(p, kind, QRectF(4, 4, 64, 64), disabled=True))
              for x, y, name in _MARK_SHOWS[kind]:
                  want = "paper" if name in _MARK_INNER else "disabled_ink"
                  assert _at(image, 4 + 4 * x, 4 + 4 * y) == design.hex_colour(want), (kind, dark, ratio, x, y, name)
              assert design.hex_colour("paper") != design.hex_colour("disabled_ink")


  def test_a_marker_stays_inside_its_box_and_an_unknown_kind_paints_nothing():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      for ratio, kind in itertools.product(_SCALINGS, paint.MARKERS + paint.GLYPHS + ("tick",)):
          image = _screen(24, 24, ratio, draw=lambda p: paint.paint_marker(p, kind, QRectF(4, 4, 16, 16)))   # as on a page
          low, high = int(4 * ratio), int(20 * ratio)
          touched = [(x, y) for y in range(image.height()) for x in range(image.width())
                     if image.pixelColor(x, y) != _BLANK]
          assert all(low <= x < high and low <= y < high for x, y in touched), (kind, ratio)
          assert bool(touched) == (kind != "tick"), (kind, ratio)


  def test_fill_px_lays_whole_device_pixels_from_the_edge_named_at_every_position():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      ink = QColor(26, 26, 26)
      # the four scalings, and two that lie between and beyond them: a weight is rounded DOWN to whole
      # device pixels there too, and is never none
      heavy, hair = {**_HEAVY_RULE, 1.75: 3, 2.5: 5}, {**_HAIR_RULE, 1.75: 1, 2.5: 2}
      bar = {1.0: 4, 1.25: 5, 1.5: 6, 1.75: 7, 2.0: 8, 2.5: 10}
      for ratio, (weight, want), position, side in itertools.product(
              sorted(bar), ((2, heavy), (1, hair), (4, bar)), range(24), ("top", "bottom", "left", "right")):
          across = side in ("top", "bottom")
          rect = QRectF(5, position, 30, 11) if across else QRectF(position, 5, 11, 30)
          image = _screen(48, 48, ratio, draw=lambda p: paint.fill_px(p, rect, ink, **{side: weight}))
          middle = int(20 * ratio)
          run = _run_of(image, ink, column=middle) if across else _run_of(image, ink, row=middle)
          first = _device_edge(position * ratio) if side in ("top", "left") else _device_edge((position + 11) * ratio) - want[ratio]
          assert run == list(range(first, first + want[ratio])), (ratio, weight, side, position, run)

      def frame(painter):
          painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.Antialiasing, True)      # a caller's painter may be smoothing
          painter.translate(0, 0.3)                               # and may stand between two pixels
          paint.fill_px(painter, QRectF(5, 5, 30, 20), ink, top=1, bottom=1, left=1, right=1)

      for ratio in sorted(bar):
          pixels = _every_pixel(_screen(48, 48, ratio, draw=frame))
          assert {pixel.rgb() for pixel in pixels} == {ink.rgb(), _BLANK.rgb()}, ratio        # no blended pixel
          n, wide, high = hair[ratio], _device_edge(35 * ratio) - _device_edge(5 * ratio), _device_edge(25.3 * ratio) - _device_edge(5.3 * ratio)
          assert pixels.count(ink) == wide * high - (wide - 2 * n) * (high - 2 * n), ratio     # each corner once, the inside bare

      def smaller(painter):
          painter.scale(0.4, 0.4)                                 # a drawing made smaller: 1 px is 0.4 of a device pixel
          paint.fill_px(painter, QRectF(10, 10, 60, 40), ink, top=1, left=1)

      small = _screen(48, 48, 1.0, draw=smaller)
      assert (_run_of(small, ink, column=10), _run_of(small, ink, row=10)) == ([4], [4])   # one device pixel each, never none
      nothing = _screen(48, 48, 1.5, draw=lambda p: paint.fill_px(p, QRectF(5, 5, 30, 20), ink))
      assert all(pixel == _BLANK for pixel in _every_pixel(nothing))                               # no edge named, nothing painted


  def test_the_hatching_stays_in_its_rectangle_and_does_not_move_with_it():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      for dark, ratio in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS):
          with theme(dark):
              paper, hatch = design.colour("paper"), design.colour("hatch")

              def hatched(painter):
                  paint.paint_hatch(painter, QRectF(10, 4, 212, 12), hatch)
                  assert not painter.hasClipping() and not painter.testRenderHint(QPainter.Antialiasing)   # left as found

              image = _screen(240, 20, ratio, paper, hatched)
              left, right, top, bottom = int(10 * ratio), math.ceil(222 * ratio), int(4 * ratio), math.ceil(16 * ratio)
              assert all(image.pixelColor(x, y) == paper for y in range(image.height()) for x in range(image.width())
                         if not (left <= x < right and top <= y < bottom)), (dark, ratio)
              row = [image.pixelColor(x, int(10 * ratio)).red() for x in range(image.width())]
              strokes = sum(1 for i, red in enumerate(row) if red != paper.red() and (i == 0 or row[i - 1] == paper.red()))
              assert strokes in (29, 30, 31), (dark, ratio, strokes)  # one every 5 px ACROSS the stroke: 212 / (5 x root 2) = 29.98
              low, high = sorted((paper.red(), hatch.red()))
              assert all(low - 1 <= red <= high + 1 for red in row)   # the two colours and their mixtures, nothing else
              assert max(abs(red - paper.red()) for red in row) >= 0.9 * (high - low), (dark, ratio)
              # A range is hatched twice on the time axis, ahead of the elapsed bar and through it: the strokes
              # of two rectangles with one top and one height fall on each other wherever both are.
              wide, narrow = (_screen(240, 20, ratio, paper, lambda p: paint.paint_hatch(p, QRectF(x0, 4, 160 - x0, 12), hatch))
                              for x0 in (10, 47))
              worst = max(abs(wide.pixelColor(x, y).red() - narrow.pixelColor(x, y).red())
                          for y in range(int(4 * ratio) + 1, int(16 * ratio) - 1)
                          for x in range(math.ceil(48 * ratio) + 1, int(160 * ratio) - 1))
              assert worst <= 8, (dark, ratio, worst)     # smoothing rounds by a level or two; a moved stroke by over a hundred
      for width in (0, -5):
          empty = _screen(40, 20, 1.0, draw=lambda p: paint.paint_hatch(p, QRectF(10, 4, width, 12), QColor(77, 77, 77)))
          assert all(pixel == _BLANK for pixel in _every_pixel(empty))

  def test_a_ruled_block_paints_whole_rules_from_its_own_edges_in_both_themes_at_four_scalings():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      for dark, ratio in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS):
          with theme(dark):
              block, child = Ruled(top=2, bottom=2), QWidget()        # what a block holds never covers its rules
              child.setAutoFillBackground(True)
              look = child.palette()
              look.setColor(child.backgroundRole(), QColor(0, 255, 0))
              child.setPalette(look)
              block.box.addWidget(child)
              block.resize(60, 31)                                    # 31: at 1.25 and 1.5 its foot falls inside a pixel
              block.layout().activate()
              column, n, foot = int(30 * ratio), _HEAVY_RULE[ratio], _device_edge(31 * ratio)
              assert _run_of(_screen_of(block, ratio), design.colour("rule"), column=column) == [*range(n), *range(foot - n, foot)], (dark, ratio)
              quiet = Ruled(top=1, colour="rule_light")
              quiet.resize(60, 31)
              assert _run_of(_screen_of(quiet, ratio), design.colour("rule_light"), column=column) == [*range(_HAIR_RULE[ratio])], (dark, ratio)
      spaced = Ruled(top=2, bottom=1, gap_top=7, gap_bottom=3)    # held in a name: its layout goes when it does
      room = spaced.box.contentsMargins()
      assert (room.left(), room.top(), room.right(), room.bottom(), spaced.box.spacing()) == (0, 9, 0, 4, 0)
      with pytest.raises(ValueError):                             # a colour is named when the block is built, not when it paints
          Ruled(top=1, colour="grey")
      plain = Ruled()
      plain.resize(20, 20)
      assert all(pixel == _BLANK for pixel in _every_pixel(_screen_of(plain, 1.0)))


  def test_a_section_heading_is_sixteen_pixels_semibold_over_a_heavy_rule_six_pixels_under_it():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      with text_size(1.0):                                        # the sizes below are those of the ordinary text size
          head = SectionHead("Main settings")
          font = head.label.font()
          assert (head.label.text(), font.pixelSize(), font.weight()) == ("Main settings", 16, QFont.Weight.DemiBold)
          assert head.label.property("cls") == "head" and head.label.textFormat() == Qt.PlainText   # a name may hold "<" or "&"
          assert head.sizeHint().height() == 22 + 6 + 2           # the heading's line, the gap, the rule
          head.resize(600, 30)
          head.layout().activate()
          for dark, ratio in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS):
              with theme(dark):
                  image, n, foot = _screen_of(head, ratio), _HEAVY_RULE[ratio], _device_edge(30 * ratio)
                  # read at the far right, where no letter stands: in the light theme a letter has the rule's colour
                  assert _run_of(image, design.colour("rule"), column=image.width() - 3) == [*range(foot - n, foot)], (dark, ratio)
          aside = QWidget()                                       # of a fixed size: no width of lettering is read
          aside.setFixedSize(40, 12)
          head.add_right(aside)
          head.layout().activate()
          assert (aside.geometry().right(), aside.geometry().bottom()) == (599, 21)     # at the right, on the heading's foot
          head.set_text("This training")
          assert head.label.text() == "This training"
      with text_size(1.25):                                       # lengths grow with the text; the rule does not
          assert SectionHead("Main settings").sizeHint().height() == 28 + 8 + 2

  def test_a_painted_icon_is_sharp_at_every_scaling_follows_the_theme_and_greys_when_disabled():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      square = {1.0: 100, 1.25: 144, 1.5: 196, 2.0: 400}          # the 10-unit square of "stop" in whole device pixels
      icon = painted_icon("stop")
      gc.collect()                                                # the engine lives on with no name of its own
      assert not icon.isNull()
      for dark, ratio in itertools.product((False, True), _SCALINGS):
          with theme(dark):
              pixmap = icon.pixmap(QSize(16, 16), ratio)
              assert (pixmap.width(), pixmap.devicePixelRatio()) == (math.ceil(16 * ratio), ratio)
              picture = pixmap.toImage()
              assert picture.pixelColor(0, 0).alpha() == 0 and _every_pixel(picture).count(design.colour("err")) == square[ratio]
              for mode, name in ((QIcon.Normal, "err"), (QIcon.Disabled, "disabled_ink")):
                  image = _screen(32, 24, ratio, draw=lambda p: icon.paint(p, QRect(4, 4, 20, 16), Qt.AlignCenter, mode, QIcon.Off))
                  # a wider icon keeps the glyph at its left: the room before a button's words stays bare
                  assert (_at(image, 12, 12), _at(image, 22, 12)) == (design.hex_colour(name), _BARE), (dark, ratio, name)
      with theme(False):
          button = QPushButton()                                  # no words: no pixel of lettering is read
          button.setIcon(icon)
          button.setIconSize(QSize(20, 16))
          button.resize(60, 34)
          assert _every_pixel(_screen_of(button, 1.0, QColor(255, 255, 255))).count(design.colour("err")) == 100
          button.setEnabled(False)
          greyed = _every_pixel(_screen_of(button, 1.0, QColor(255, 255, 255)))
          assert greyed.count(design.colour("err")) == 0 and greyed.count(design.colour("disabled_ink")) >= 100
      with pytest.raises(ValueError):
          painted_icon("tick")


  def test_a_painted_icon_never_ends_the_process():
      """In an interpreter of its own, because each fault here ends the whole process, which would be
      the test run itself. When a copy of an icon is changed the toolkit asks the icon's engine for a
      twin, and a twin that nothing keeps alive ends the process. So does an engine whose drawing raises
      while its painter still paints on the picture it is making."""
      code = "\n".join((
          "import gc",
          "from PySide6.QtCore import QRect, QSize",
          "from PySide6.QtGui import QIcon, QImage, QPainter, QPixmap",
          "from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication",
          "app = QApplication([])",
          "from core.gui import paint",
          "from core.gui.widgets.marker import painted_icon",
          "icon = painted_icon('stop'); copy = QIcon(icon); copy.addPixmap(QPixmap(8, 8)); gc.collect()",
          "image = QImage(32, 32, QImage.Format_ARGB32_Premultiplied); image.fill(0); painter = QPainter(image)",
          "icon.paint(painter, QRect(0, 0, 16, 16)); copy.paint(painter, QRect(16, 16, 16, 16)); painter.end()",
          "print(image.pixelColor(8, 8).name(), image.pixelColor(24, 24).name())",
          "del icon, copy; gc.collect()",
          "def broken(*args, **kwargs): raise KeyError('a colour the table lacks')",
          "paint.paint_marker = broken",
          "try:",
          "    painted_icon('stop').pixmap(QSize(16, 16))",
          "except KeyError:",
          "    print('raised')",
          "gc.collect()"))
      done = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-u", "-c", code], cwd=str(REPO),
                            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)     # -u: what was printed before a fault is kept
      vermilion = design.hex_colour("err", False).lower()
      assert (done.returncode, done.stdout.split()) == (0, [vermilion, vermilion, "raised"]), \
          (done.returncode, done.stdout, done.stderr[-2000:])
  ```

  ```python
  import contextlib
  import dataclasses
  import math

  import pytest
  from PySide6.QtCore import QCoreApplication, QEvent, QPoint, Qt
  from PySide6.QtGui import QFontMetricsF, QPainter, QPalette
  from PySide6.QtTest import QTest
  from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QVBoxLayout, QWidget

  from core.gui import design, fonts

  SCALINGS = (1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0)

  def _rt():
      QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])    # a widget needs the application, whichever test runs first
      from core.gui.widgets import rule_table        # inside each test: until the module exists only these fail
      return rule_table

  def _settle():
      for _ in range(4):
          QApplication.sendPostedEvents()
          QApplication.processEvents()

  @contextlib.contextmanager
  def _the_look(dark, sheet=True):
      """One theme in force, its palette on the application and its sheet too unless that is left out; all three
      put back, whatever the block does."""
      app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
      was_sheet, was_palette = app.styleSheet(), QPalette(app.palette())
      with theme(dark):
          try:
              app.setPalette(design.build_palette(dark))
              if sheet:
                  app.setStyleSheet(design.build_qss(dark))
              yield
          finally:
              app.setStyleSheet(was_sheet)
              app.setPalette(was_palette)

  def _gone(widget):
      """Delete a widget now. Asked only to delete itself later it would stay to the end of the run: no event
      loop turns between two tests. This widget's own request is delivered, and nobody else's."""
      widget.deleteLater()
      QCoreApplication.sendPostedEvents(widget, QEvent.DeferredDelete)

  @contextlib.contextmanager
  def _on_a_page(table, width=500, height=400):
      """The table as a page holds it: alone in a column, with room to spare under it. The page is shown where no
      screen sees it and is never the active window; it goes, with the table in it, when the block ends."""
      page = QWidget()
      column = QVBoxLayout(page)
      column.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
      column.addWidget(table)
      page.resize(width, height)
      page.setAttribute(Qt.WA_DontShowOnScreen, True)
      page.setAttribute(Qt.WA_ShowWithoutActivating, True)
      try:
          page.show()
          _settle()
          yield page
      finally:
          page.close()
          _gone(page)

  def _blank(rows=3, **options):
      """Columns 120 wide, stretching and 110 wide, and no lettering anywhere: no pixel read off it is a letter's."""
      rt = _rt()
      columns = [rt.Column("", 120), rt.Column(""), rt.Column("", 110, right=True)]
      return rt.RuleTable(columns, [[rt.TextCell(""), rt.TextCell(""), rt.ValueCell("")]] * rows, **options)

  def _rendered(widget, ratio):
      """The widget, its own ground with it, drawn at a display scaling. The painter is ended whatever the drawing
      does: a picture let go under a live painter ends the whole run, where the test should only fail."""
      image = _image(widget.width(), widget.height(), ratio)
      painter = QPainter(image)
      try:
          widget.render(painter, QPoint(0, 0))
      finally:
          painter.end()
      return image

  def _down(image, x):
      """One column of device pixels, top to bottom, as (pixel, how many in a run)."""
      runs = []
      for y in range(image.height()):
          pixel = image.pixel(x, y)
          if runs and runs[-1][0] == pixel:
              runs[-1][1] += 1
          else:
              runs.append([pixel, 1])
      return [(pixel, n) for pixel, n in runs]

  def _pixels(image):
      return {image.pixel(x, y) for y in range(image.height()) for x in range(image.width())}

  def _marked(image, x0, x1, ground, ratio):
      """Where the header's line of words holds a mark between two x of the table: for each device row, its
      first and last marked x. The rules above and below the header are left out."""
      rows = {}
      for y in range(math.ceil(2 * ratio) + 1, int(28 * ratio) - 1):
          xs = [x for x in range(int(x0 * ratio), int(x1 * ratio)) if image.pixel(x, y) != ground]
          if xs:
              rows[y] = (xs[0], xs[-1])
      return rows
  ```

  def test_a_tables_three_rules_are_whole_device_pixels_at_every_scaling():
      weights = {1.0: [2, 1, 2], 1.25: [2, 1, 2], 1.5: [3, 1, 3], 2.0: [4, 2, 4]}
      for dark in (False, True):
          with _the_look(dark):
              table = _blank(selectable=False)
              with _on_a_page(table):
                  rule = design.colour("rule").rgb()
                  for ratio, expected in weights.items():
                      image = _rendered(table, ratio)
                      for x in (1, image.width() // 2, image.width() - 2):
                          found = [n for pixel, n in _down(image, x) if pixel == rule]
                          assert found == expected, (dark, ratio, x, found)

  def test_a_table_is_as_tall_as_its_rows_and_stands_on_the_page():

  def test_a_selected_row_has_its_tint_a_line_above_and_below_and_a_bar():
      lines = {1.0: 1, 1.25: 1, 1.5: 1, 2.0: 2}
      bars = {1.0: 4, 1.25: 5, 1.5: 6, 2.0: 8}

                      assert column[first][1] == column[first + 2][1] == lines[ratio], (dark, ratio)

                      tall = sum(n for _, n in column[first:first + 3])

  def test_a_fitted_column_measures_every_kind_of_cell_and_stops_at_its_limit():
      rt = _rt()

      def fitted(cells, title="", sortable=False):
          """The width of a fitted column that is neither first nor last: no lead, a gap of 16 after it."""
          table = rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("", 50), rt.Column(title, "fit"), rt.Column("")],
                               [[rt.TextCell(""), cell, rt.TextCell("")] for cell in cells], sortable=sortable)
          width = table.header.sectionSize(1)
          _gone(table)
          return width

      figure = QFontMetricsF(fonts.inter("strong")).horizontalAdvance("20,480,000")
      word = QFontMetricsF(fonts.inter("body")).horizontalAdvance("Done")
      assert fitted([rt.TextCell("")]) == 20                            # nothing to hold: a column's least width
      assert 16 + figure < fitted([rt.ValueCell("20,480,000", "simulations")]) <= 16 + 180
      assert fitted([rt.ValueCell("1", second="of 10,000 batches")]) > fitted([rt.ValueCell("1")])
      assert fitted([rt.StateCell("done", "Done")]) >= 16 + 16 + 6 + math.floor(word)      # gap, marker, its gap
      assert fitted([rt.TextCell("a")]) < fitted([rt.TextCell("a"), rt.TextCell("a longer name")])
      assert fitted([rt.TextCell("x" * 200)]) == 16 + 180              # at most 180, then the gap
      assert fitted([rt.TextCell("")], "Made", sortable=True) - fitted([rt.TextCell("")], "Made") == 4 + 16

      table = rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("", "fit"), rt.Column("")], [[rt.TextCell("x" * 200), rt.TextCell("")]])
      assert table.header.sectionSize(0) == 10 + 180 + 16              # the first column also leads by 10
      table.set_rows([[rt.TextCell(""), rt.TextCell("")]])             # rows set later are measured again
      assert table.header.sectionSize(0) == 10 + 16
      _gone(table)

      table = rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("", 50), rt.Column("", "fit"), rt.Column("")], [[rt.TextCell("")] * 3])
      assert table.view.minimumWidth() == 50 + 20 + 40                 # the view's own two widths (the fitted one held
      _gone(table)                                                     # to a column's least) and a stretching column's least

  def test_a_header_that_sorts_starts_with_no_column_sorted_and_paints_a_chevron_after_the_words():
      click = (Qt.LeftButton, Qt.NoModifier, QPoint(200, 10))           # inside the middle column's header
      for dark in (False, True):
          with _the_look(dark):
              plain, table = _blank(), _blank(sortable=True)
              with _on_a_page(plain), _on_a_page(table):
                  paper = design.colour("paper").rgb()
                  unheard, heard = [], []
                  plain.header.sortIndicatorChanged.connect(lambda column, order: unheard.append((column, order)))
                  table.header.sortIndicatorChanged.connect(lambda column, order: heard.append((column, order)))
                  QTest.mouseClick(plain.header.viewport(), *click)
                  assert plain.header.sectionsClickable() is False and unheard == []
                  assert table.header.sortIndicatorSection() == -1     # the toolkit's own header starts at column 0
                  assert table.view.isSortingEnabled() is False        # the toolkit never sorts the rows itself
                  assert _marked(_rendered(table, 1.0), 0, 500, paper, 1.0) == {}
                  table.select_row(2)
                  before = [table.view.model().index(r, 0).data(Qt.UserRole) for r in range(3)]
                  QTest.mouseClick(table.header.viewport(), *click)
                  assert heard == [(1, Qt.AscendingOrder)]
                  for ratio in SCALINGS:
                      image = _rendered(table, ratio)
                      rows = _marked(image, 120, 390, paper, ratio)
                      assert rows and not _marked(image, 0, 120, paper, ratio)
                      assert not _marked(image, 390, 500, paper, ratio)
                      top, bottom = rows[min(rows)], rows[max(rows)]
                      assert top[1] - top[0] < bottom[1] - bottom[0], (dark, ratio)        # smallest first: it points up

                  QTest.mouseClick(table.header.viewport(), *click)
                  assert heard[-1] == (1, Qt.DescendingOrder)
                  tall = {}
                  for ratio in SCALINGS:
                      rows = _marked(_rendered(table, ratio), 120, 390, paper, ratio)
                      top, bottom = rows[min(rows)], rows[max(rows)]
                      assert top[1] - top[0] > bottom[1] - bottom[0], (dark, ratio)        # largest first: it points down
                      tall[ratio] = len(rows)

                  table.header.setSortIndicator(2, Qt.DescendingOrder)  # set from code, as a page restores an order
                  for ratio in SCALINGS:
                      image = _rendered(table, ratio)
                      assert not _marked(image, 0, 390, paper, ratio)
                      assert len(_marked(image, 390, 500, paper, ratio)) == tall[ratio]    # whole, inside the last column

                  # the header says which column and which way; the rows and the selection are the page's
                  assert [table.view.model().index(r, 0).data(Qt.UserRole) for r in range(3)] == before
                  assert table.selected_row() == 2

  def test_the_current_row_wears_its_own_ring_clear_of_the_bar():
      still = _blank(selectable=False)
      assert still.view.focusPolicy() == Qt.NoFocus
      _gone(still)
      top = 2 + 27 + 30                                                 # where the second row begins
      # The ring is 2 wide, 2 inside the row's edge and right of the bar of 4. Read where no scaling blurs it:
      # the middle of each of its four sides, and a point on either side of each that it must leave alone.
      sides = ((250, top + 3), (250, top + 27), (7, top + 15), (497, top + 15))
      beside = ((250, top + 0.5), (250, top + 5.5), (250, top + 24.5), (250, top + 29.5),
                (5, top + 15), (9.5, top + 15), (494.5, top + 15), (499.5, top + 15))
      for dark in (False, True):
          with _the_look(dark):
              table = _blank()
              with _on_a_page(table):
                  assert table.view.focusPolicy() == Qt.StrongFocus
                  table.select_row(1)
                  _settle()
                  focus, accent = design.hex_colour("focus"), design.hex_colour("accent")
                  for shown in (False, True, False):
                      table.view.set_focus_shown(shown)
                      _settle()
                      for ratio in SCALINGS:
                          image = _rendered(table, ratio)
                          where = (dark, shown, ratio)
                          assert [_at(image, x, y) == focus for x, y in sides] == [shown] * 4, where
                          assert not [point for point in beside if _at(image, *point) == focus], where
                          assert _at(image, 0.5, top + 15) == _at(image, 3.5, top + 15) == accent, where   # the bar is whole
                      if dark and not shown:                  # in dark the ring's colour is no other colour of a table
                          assert design.colour("focus").rgb() not in _pixels(_rendered(table, 1.0))

  def test_a_cell_is_a_plain_description_and_the_table_keeps_its_words():
      rt = _rt()
      name = rt.TextCell("retrain_posterior", elide="middle")
      count = rt.ValueCell("20,480,000", "simulations")
      state = rt.StateCell("done", "Done")
      with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
          name.text = "another"
      assert rt.TextCell("a") == rt.TextCell("a", quiet=False, elide="end", wrap=False)
      assert rt.ValueCell("1") == rt.ValueCell("1", unit="", second="")
      assert rt.Column("a") == rt.Column("a", width=None, right=False)

      table = rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("Name", "fit"), rt.Column("Holds", None, right=True), rt.Column("State", 120)],
                           [[name, count, state]])
      model = table.view.model()
      assert [model.index(0, c).data(Qt.UserRole) for c in range(3)] == [name, count, state]
      assert model.index(0, 1).data(Qt.UserRole) is count
      assert [model.index(0, c).data(Qt.DisplayRole) for c in range(3)] == [
          "retrain_posterior", "20,480,000 simulations", "Done"]
      assert [model.headerData(c, Qt.Horizontal) for c in range(3)] == ["Name", "Holds", "State"]
      assert not model.index(0, 0).flags() & Qt.ItemIsEditable
      assert isinstance(table.header, rt.RuleHeader) and table.header is table.view.horizontalHeader()
      assert isinstance(table.view.itemDelegate(), rt.RuleDelegate)
      assert rt.RuleHeader().sortable is False and rt.RuleHeader(sortable=True).sortable is True

      with pytest.raises(ValueError):
          table.set_rows([[name, count]])                               # a cell short
      with pytest.raises(TypeError):
          table.set_rows([[name, count, "Done"]])                       # words in place of a description
      with pytest.raises(ValueError):
          table.set_rows([[name, count, rt.StateCell("finished", "Finished")]])            # no such marker
      with pytest.raises(ValueError):
          rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("a"), rt.Column("b")])                # two columns cannot both take the room left
      assert model.rowCount() == 1 and model.index(0, 2).data(Qt.UserRole) is state    # a refused call changed nothing

      table.select_row(0)
      assert table.selected_row() == 0
      table.set_rows([[name, count, state], [name, count, state]])
      assert table.view.model() is model and model.rowCount() == 2      # the same model: what listens to it stays
      assert table.selected_row() is None                               # new rows, nothing selected
      with _on_a_page(table):
          QTest.mouseClick(table.view.viewport(), Qt.LeftButton, Qt.NoModifier, QPoint(200, 30 + 15))
          assert table.selected_row() == 1

  def test_a_wrapped_cell_makes_its_row_as_tall_as_its_lines_at_the_width_it_has():
      rt = _rt()
      words = " ".join(["a note that runs on"] * 12)
      table = rt.RuleTable([rt.Column("", 120), rt.Column("")],
                           [[rt.TextCell(""), rt.TextCell(words, wrap=True)], [rt.TextCell(""), rt.TextCell(words)]])
      with _on_a_page(table, width=500) as page:
          narrow = table.view.rowHeight(0)
          assert narrow > 30 and (narrow - 10) % 20 == 0                # whole lines of 20, with 5 above and below
          assert table.view.rowHeight(1) == 30                          # not wrapped: one line, cut at its end
          assert table.height() == 2 + 27 + narrow + 30 + 2
          page.resize(780, 400)
          _settle()
          wide = table.view.rowHeight(0)
          assert 30 <= wide < narrow and (wide - 10) % 20 == 0          # more room, fewer lines: measured again
          assert table.height() == 2 + 27 + wide + 30 + 2
  ```

```python
# core/gui/widgets/time_axis.py    imports: datetime, math, Callable from collections.abc, PySide6, and from core.gui: design, fonts, paint, widgets.marker
"""The time axis of a run: where everything on it goes, as plain numbers; a widget that paints only
those numbers; and the one line of words under it."""

def axis_layout(start, now, end_from, end_by, width: int, text_width: Callable[[str], float]) -> dict:
    """Where everything on the time axis goes, as plain numbers: no painter and no widget, so it is
    tested without a screen. `end_by` None: no end is known. `end_from` None, or equal to `end_by`:
    the end is firm. Given moments of one kind (all with a time zone, or all without) it never raises,
    whatever their order, and the axis is never shorter than 30 s.
    Keys: late, inside, axis_end, x_done, x_now, x_from, x_by, step, ticks, labels (pairs of x and text)."""

class TimeAxis(QWidget):
    """A run drawn on a labelled time axis: what has passed, where it stands now and the range in which
    it should end. It paints what axis_layout returns, reads every colour when it paints, and moves
    only when its page gives it new times."""
    def __init__(self, start, now, end_from=None, end_by=None, *, unknown: str = "") -> None: ...
    def set_times(self, start, now, end_from=None, end_by=None, *, unknown: str = "") -> None: ...

class AxisCaption(QWidget):
    """The one line under a time axis: when the run started and, at the right, when it should end."""
    started: QLabel; words: QLabel; key: QWidget; marker: Marker      # key: the hatched range in small
    def __init__(self, start, now, end_from=None, end_by=None, *, unknown: str = "") -> None: ...
    def set_times(self, start, now, end_from=None, end_by=None, *, unknown: str = "") -> None: ...
    # unknown: the caller's sentence for the right-hand side when no end is known, shown as written
```

def _seven(text):
    """Seven pixels a character: a measure that needs no font."""
    return 7.0 * len(text)

def _axis(*times):
    from core.gui.widgets.time_axis import axis_layout
    return axis_layout(*times, _AXIS_W, _seven)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("moment", AXIS_MOMENTS, ids=[m[0] for m in AXIS_MOMENTS])
def test_the_time_axis_layout_at_the_run_page_and_the_eight_other_moments(moment):
    _, times, step, ticks, x_done, x_now, x_from, x_by, inside, late, axis_end, labels = moment
    got = _axis(*times)
    assert sorted(got) == _AXIS_KEYS
    assert (got["step"], got["ticks"]) == (step, ticks)
    assert (got["x_done"], got["x_now"], got["x_from"], got["x_by"]) == (x_done, x_now, x_from, x_by)
    assert (got["inside"], got["late"], got["axis_end"]) == (inside, late, axis_end)
    assert [text for _, text in got["labels"]] == [text for _, text in labels]
    assert [x for x, _ in got["labels"]] == pytest.approx([x for x, _ in labels], abs=0.01)

def test_the_time_axis_layout_of_a_firm_end_has_no_range_to_hatch():
    firm = _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _FIRM, _FIRM)
    assert (firm["x_from"], firm["x_by"], firm["late"], firm["inside"]) == (1038, 1038, False, False)
    assert (firm["x_done"], firm["axis_end"], len(firm["ticks"])) == (347, _FIRM, 8)
    assert _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, None, _FIRM) == firm                    # an end with no earliest end is firm
    past = _axis(_FIT, _FIRM + _plus(hours=2), _FIRM, _FIRM)
    assert (past["late"], past["axis_end"]) == (True, _FIRM + _plus(days=1))
    assert (past["x_from"], past["x_by"], past["x_done"]) == (924, 924, 934)

def test_the_time_axis_with_no_end_known_hatches_nothing_is_never_late_and_never_spans_under_30_seconds():
    waiting = _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _EARLIEST, None)                     # to the moment before which it cannot end
    assert (waiting["axis_end"], waiting["x_done"]) == (_EARLIEST, 243)
    passed = _axis(_FIT, dt.datetime(2026, 10, 14), _EARLIEST, None)     # now has passed that moment: to now
    assert (passed["axis_end"], passed["x_done"], passed["x_now"]) == (dt.datetime(2026, 10, 14), 1038, 1035.0)
    bare = _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, None, None)                             # no such moment given: to now
    assert (bare["axis_end"], bare["x_done"]) == (_FIT_NOW, 1038)
    first = _axis(_FIT, _FIT, None, None)                                # the first instant: 30 s of axis, not none
    assert (first["axis_end"], first["step"]) == (_FIT + _plus(seconds=30), 30)
    assert (first["ticks"], first["labels"], first["x_done"], first["x_now"]) == ([], [], 0, 3.0)
    assert _axis(_FIT, _FIT + _plus(seconds=10), None, None)["x_done"] == 346
    for got in (waiting, passed, bare, first):
        assert (got["late"], got["inside"], got["x_from"], got["x_by"]) == (False, False, 1038, 1038)

def test_the_time_axis_layout_takes_odd_times_without_raising_or_leaving_the_axis():
    assert _axis(_FIT, _FIT, _FIT, _FIT)["axis_end"] == _FIT + _plus(seconds=30)         # an end at the start itself
    assert _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _FIT - _plus(hours=5), _DUE_BY)["x_from"] == 0          # an earliest end before it
    crossed = _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_BY + _plus(hours=5), _DUE_BY)                   # the two ends crossed
    assert crossed["x_from"] == crossed["x_by"] == 1038
    early = _axis(_FIT, _FIT - _plus(hours=1), _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)                       # a clock that went back
    assert (early["x_done"], early["x_now"]) == (0, 3.0)
    overdue = _axis(_FIT, _DUE_BY + _plus(days=3.2), _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)                 # 3.2 days late: four more days
    assert (overdue["late"], overdue["axis_end"]) == (True, _DUE_BY + _plus(days=4))
    assert (overdue["x_done"], overdue["x_from"], overdue["x_by"]) == (955, 519, 623)
    zone = dt.timezone(_plus(hours=-7))                                                  # times that carry a zone
    aware = _axis(*(t.replace(tzinfo=zone) for t in (_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)))
    assert (aware["x_done"], aware["ticks"]) == (470, _MIDNIGHTS)

def test_a_time_axis_tick_label_is_short_and_english_and_is_left_out_sooner_than_printed_over_its_neighbour():
    for number, name in enumerate("Jan Feb Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug Sep Oct Nov Dec".split(), 1):
        start = dt.datetime(2026, number, 2, 6, 0)
        days = _axis(start, start, start + _plus(days=3), start + _plus(days=4))["labels"]
        assert [text for _, text in days][:2] == [f"2 {name}", f"3 {name}"]
        clock = _axis(start, start, start + _plus(hours=30), start + _plus(hours=40))["labels"]
        assert [text for _, text in clock] == ["12:00", "18:00", f"3 {name} 00:00", "06:00", "12:00", "18:00"]
    crowded = _axis(_FIT, dt.datetime(2026, 10, 14), _EARLIEST, None)["labels"]
    assert [text for _, text in crowded][:3] == ["1 Oct", "3 Oct", "4 Oct"]              # "2 Oct" would touch "1 Oct"
    for moment in AXIS_MOMENTS:
        labels = _axis(*moment[1])["labels"]
        for (x, text), (following, _) in zip(labels, labels[1:]):
            assert following >= x + _seven(text) + 8, moment[0]
        assert all(0 <= x <= _AXIS_W - _seven(text) for x, text in labels), moment[0]

def test_the_time_axis_takes_its_months_from_the_looks_table(monkeypatch):
    source = (REPO / "core" / "gui" / "widgets" / "time_axis.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    called = {node.func.attr for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(source))
              if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute)}
    assert "strftime" not in called        # a month or a weekday asked of the system follows the regional setting
    monkeypatch.setattr(design, "MONTHS", tuple("abcdefghijkl"))         # one letter where each month stands
    days = _axis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)["labels"]
    assert [text for _, text in days][:2] == ["1 j", "2 j"]              # the tenth, read when the tick is written

def _axis_image(widget, ratio, width=None):
    """The widget alone (made `width` wide first), drawn into a clear picture of that display scaling."""
    if width:
        widget.resize(width, widget.height())
    image = _image(widget.width(), widget.height(), ratio)                # its size rounded up
    widget.render(image, QPoint(), QRegion(), QWidget.RenderFlag.DrawChildren)    # no ground of its own, no painter held
    return image

def _axis_rgb(name):
    return design.colour(name).rgb()

def _axis_stroked(image, ratio, x0, x1, ground):
    """For each device column of the logical span x0 to x1: is any pixel inside the track not `ground`?"""
    top, height = design.AXIS["track_y"], design.AXIS["track_h"]
    rows = range(math.ceil((top + 1) * ratio) + 1, math.floor((top + height - 1) * ratio) - 1)
    return [any(image.pixel(dx, dy) != ground for dy in rows)
            for dx in range(math.ceil(x0 * ratio), math.floor(x1 * ratio))]

@pytest.mark.parametrize("ratio", [1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("dark", [False, True], ids=["light", "dark"])
def test_the_time_axis_hatching_lies_exactly_between_the_two_end_estimates_and_nowhere_without_two(dark, ratio):
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])                 # before any widget: a run may begin at this test
    from core.gui.widgets.time_axis import TimeAxis
    with theme(dark):
        paper, bar, rule = _axis_rgb("paper"), _axis_rgb("elapsed"), _axis_rgb("rule")
        for name, times in [moment[:2] for moment in AXIS_MOMENTS] + AXIS_WITHOUT_A_RANGE:
            image, lay = _axis_image(TimeAxis(*times), ratio, _AXIS_W), _axis(*times)
            x_from, x_by, x_done = lay["x_from"], lay["x_by"], lay["x_done"]
            left, right = lay["x_now"] - 4, lay["x_now"] + 4          # the mark, its halo and a pixel to spare
            reached = lay["late"] or lay["inside"]                    # the bar has reached the range
            behind = min(x_done, left, x_from if reached else _AXIS_W) - 1
            assert not any(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, 2, behind, bar)), name
            if reached:
                assert all(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, x_from + 1, min(x_done, x_by, left) - 1, bar)), name
            if lay["late"]:
                assert not any(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, x_by + 1, left - 1, bar)), name
                assert not any(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, right + 1, _AXIS_W - 1, paper)), name
            else:
                assert not any(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, max(x_done, right) + 1, x_from - 1, paper)), name
                assert all(_axis_stroked(image, ratio, max(x_from + 1, right), _AXIS_W - 1, paper)), name
            if not reached and x_from < _AXIS_W:                      # the range begins on one whole device pixel
                assert image.pixel(math.floor(x_from * ratio + 0.5), int(11 * ratio)) == rule, name

@pytest.mark.parametrize("ratio, weight", [(1.0, 1), (1.25, 1), (1.5, 1), (2.0, 2)])
def test_the_time_axis_track_is_outlined_on_whole_device_pixels_and_the_now_mark_stands_through_it(ratio, weight):
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])                 # before any widget: a run may begin at this test
    from core.gui.widgets.time_axis import TimeAxis
    for dark in (False, True):
        with theme(dark):
            rule, accent, paper = _axis_rgb("rule"), _axis_rgb("accent"), _axis_rgb("paper")
            images = {x: _axis_image(TimeAxis(_FIT, now, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY), ratio, _AXIS_W)     # the first instant,
                      for now, x in ((_FIT, 3), (_FIT_NOW, 470), (_DUE_BY, 1035))}              # the middle, the last
            for x, image in images.items():
                for y in (1, 11, 20):                                            # above the track, in it, below it
                    across = {image.pixel(dx, int(y * ratio))
                              for dx in range(math.ceil((x - 2) * ratio), math.floor((x + 2) * ratio))}
                    assert across == {accent}, (dark, x, y)
                    for beside in (x - 2.5, x + 2.5):        # a pixel of the page each side, over the bar and the outline too
                        assert image.pixel(math.floor(beside * ratio), int(y * ratio)) == paper, (dark, x, y, beside)
            # at the middle moment, a column ahead of the bar, before the range and on no tick, read
            # from the top to the track's foot only: the lettering below it is never read
            column = [images[470].pixel(int(600 * ratio), dy) for dy in range(int(22 * ratio))]
            runs = [(colour, len(list(run))) for colour, run in itertools.groupby(column)]
            assert [n for colour, n in runs if colour == rule] == [weight, weight], (dark, runs)
            # the row under the track and over the lettering: the six midnights, one hairline each, and no other rule
            row = [images[470].pixel(dx, int(20.5 * ratio)) for dx in range(images[470].width())]
            assert all(row[math.floor(x * ratio + 0.5)] == rule for x in _MIDNIGHTS), dark
            assert row.count(rule) == len(_MIDNIGHTS) * weight, (dark, row.count(rule))

def test_the_time_axis_grows_with_the_text_size_and_its_mark_keeps_its_width():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])                 # before any widget: a run may begin at this test
    from core.gui.widgets.time_axis import TimeAxis
    for factor, height, mark, second in ((1.0, 42, 22, "2 Oct"), (1.25, 53, 28, "3 Oct"), (2.0, 84, 44, "3 Oct")):
        with text_size(factor):
            crowded = _axis(_FIT, dt.datetime(2026, 10, 13, 17, 0), None, None)["labels"]
            assert crowded[1][1] == second          # the room kept between two labels grows too: 8, 10, 16
            # now on a midnight, at 382: the day names stand between midnights, so the column read
            # below crosses no lettering; and the tick that falls there must not cut the mark
            axis = TimeAxis(_FIT, dt.datetime(2026, 10, 4), _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)
            image, accent = _axis_image(axis, 1.0, _AXIS_W), _axis_rgb("accent")
            assert axis.height() == height
            assert sum(image.pixel(382, dy) == accent for dy in range(height)) == mark      # as tall as its track needs
            assert sum(image.pixel(dx, 1) == accent for dx in range(_AXIS_W)) == 4          # and no wider

def test_the_line_under_the_time_axis_and_its_spoken_name_say_when_the_run_started_and_should_end():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])                 # before any widget
    from core.gui.widgets.time_axis import AxisCaption, TimeAxis
    line, axis = AxisCaption(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY), TimeAxis(_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY)
    assert line.started.text() == "Started Thu 1 Oct, 19:02"
    assert axis.accessibleName() == ("Started Thu 1 Oct, 19:02. "
                                     "Expected to end between Tue 6 Oct, 19:00 and Wed 7 Oct, 19:00.")
    waiting = "No end time yet: the first batches are being timed."
    for times, unknown, words, key, marker in (
            ((_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY), "", "Expected to end between Tue 6 Oct, 19:00 and Wed 7 Oct, 19:00",
             True, False),
            ((_FIT, dt.datetime(2026, 10, 7, 1, 45), _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY), "", "Expected to end by Wed 7 Oct, 19:00",
             True, False),                                                       # inside the range
            ((_FIT, _FIT + _plus(hours=153), _DUE_FROM, _DUE_BY), "",
             "Later than expected: it was due by Wed 7 Oct, 19:00", False, True),
            ((_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _FIRM, _FIRM), "", "Expected to end by Fri 9 Oct, 22:00", False, False),  # no range, no key
            ((_FIT, _FIT_NOW, None, None), waiting, waiting, False, False),
            ((_FIT, _FIT_NOW, _EARLIEST, None), "a <b>name</b> & more", "a <b>name</b> & more", False, False),
            ((_FIT, _FIT_NOW, None, None), "", "", False, False)):
        line.set_times(*times, unknown=unknown)
        axis.set_times(*times, unknown=unknown)
        assert (line.words.text(), not line.key.isHidden(), not line.marker.isHidden()) == (words, key, marker)
        spoken = "Started Thu 1 Oct, 19:02." + (" " + words.rstrip(".") + "." if words else "")
        assert axis.accessibleName() == spoken
    assert line.marker.kind == "warn"
    assert line.words.textFormat() == Qt.PlainText and line.started.textFormat() == Qt.PlainText   # shown as written

The forms are tried in THIS order and the first that holds is taken (so no row ever reads an `end_by` that is None, and an end given with no earliest end reads as firm):

| form | when | the right-hand words | beside them |
|---|---|---|---|
| no end | `end_by` is None | `unknown`, as given | nothing |
| late | `now > end_by` | "Later than expected: it was due by {end_by}" | `Marker("warn")` |
| firm | `end_from` is None or equals `end_by` | "Expected to end by {end_by}" | nothing: no range is hatched, so no key |
| inside | `end_from <= now` | "Expected to end by {end_by}" | the key |
| ahead | otherwise | "Expected to end between {end_from} and {end_by}" | the key |

```python
# core/gui/widgets/page.py        imports: html, math, PySide6, and from core.gui: design, fonts
def bold_weight(family: str) -> int:
    """The weight to ask for bold in a face: 600 in the lettering face, whose two files end there, 700 in a book face."""
class Sentence(QLabel):
    """One sentence in the book face, set at a fixed line height. Its text is shown as written: nothing in it
    is read as markup. The opening words may be bold; a quiet sentence is set in the second ink."""
    def __init__(self, text: str = "", *, quiet: bool = False) -> None: ...
    def set_text(self, text: str, *, lead: str | None = None) -> None: ...   # lead: the bold opening words; None drops them
    def plain_text(self) -> str: ...                                         # the lead, a space, the text: what is shown
    def retheme(self) -> None: ...                                           # writes the text again in the colours now in force
class PageHead(QWidget):
    """A page's heading: its title, one sentence under it in the book face, its actions at the right."""
    title: QLabel; sentence: Sentence
    def __init__(self, title: str, sentence: str = "") -> None: ...
    def add_action(self, button: QAbstractButton) -> None: ...               # in the order added, left to right, at the top
    def set_sentence(self, text: str) -> None: ...
    def set_small(self, small: bool) -> None: ...                            # the low window: the sentence goes
class Scroller(QScrollArea):
    """The middle of a page. It scrolls when the window is too low for what it holds, keeps the room a focus
    ring needs round it, and tells it how wide the page is, so that two columns can become one."""
    body: QWidget
    def __init__(self, body: QWidget) -> None: ...
class Columns(QWidget):
    """Two blocks side by side while the page is wide enough for both, one above the other when it is not."""
    box: QBoxLayout
    def __init__(self, left: QWidget, right: QWidget, *, stretch: tuple[int, int] = (1, 1),
                 gap: int | None = None, gap_stacked: int | None = None) -> None: ...
    def fit(self, width: int) -> None: ...
    def stacked(self) -> bool: ...
class Page(QWidget):
    """A page of the program: parts that stay where they are and a middle that scrolls."""
    box: QVBoxLayout
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...
    def add_fixed(self, part: QWidget | QLayout) -> None: ...                # set in by the ring's room, so it lines up with the middle
    def add_gap(self, usual: int, small: int | None = None) -> None: ...     # a space the low window may shorten
    def add_scrolling(self, body: QWidget) -> Scroller: ...                  # stretch 1
    def set_small(self, small: bool) -> None: ...
    def is_small(self) -> bool: ...
    def first_focus(self) -> QWidget | None: ...                             # None here; a page with settings answers its first

# core/gui/widgets/message_row.py   imports: datetime, PySide6, and from core.gui: design, paint; .marker.Marker; .page.Sentence
def opening(lead: str | None, when: datetime | None, now: datetime | None = None) -> str:
    """The bold opening of a message: its lead word, its date when it has one, and a full stop."""
class MessageRow(QWidget):
    """A marker and one sentence in the book face whose opening words are bold. An error has an edge at its left."""
    kind: str; marker: Marker | None; sentence: Sentence      # kind: one of paint.MARKERS, or "" for no marker
    def __init__(self, kind: str, sentence: str, *, lead: str | None = None,
                 when: datetime | None = None, now: datetime | None = None) -> None: ...
```

```python
# the page devices
BOOK_FACE_MODULES = ("core/gui/widgets/message_row.py", "core/gui/widgets/page.py")
SENTENCE_LINES = {16: 22}      # a sentence's pixel size and its line height, in a book face or, with none, the lettering's

def _shown_text(label):
    """What a rich-text label shows, as plain text."""
    document = QTextDocument()
    document.setHtml(label.text())
    return document.toPlainText()

def _least(width=0, height=0):
    widget = QWidget()
    widget.setMinimumSize(width, height)
    return widget

def test_a_sentence_shows_its_text_as_written():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import page
    text = 'Set {name} to <b>3 & 4</b>, not {0}; "two  spaces".\nA second line.'
    label = page.Sentence(text)
    assert _shown_text(label) == text == label.plain_text()
    label.set_text(text, lead="Lead & <co>.")
    assert _shown_text(label) == "Lead & <co>. " + text == label.plain_text()
    assert "<b>" not in label.text() and "&lt;b&gt;" in label.text() and "&amp;" in label.text()
    label.set_text("")
    assert label.text() == "" == label.plain_text()

def test_a_sentence_is_a_whole_number_of_lines_of_one_fixed_height():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import page
    assert design.text_scale() == 1.0, "a text factor leaked into this suite"
    label = page.Sentence("One line.")
    assert label.wordWrap() and label.textFormat() == Qt.TextFormat.RichText
    size = label.font().pixelSize()
    assert size == fonts.book().pixelSize() == 16, "a sentence is set 16 on 22 in whichever face it gets"
    line = SENTENCE_LINES[size]
    assert line == 22 and f"line-height:{line}px" in label.text()
    assert label.sizeHint().height() == line == label.heightForWidth(2000)
    assert page.Sentence("One.\nTwo.").heightForWidth(2000) == 2 * line
    height = page.Sentence("word " * 60).heightForWidth(200)
    assert height >= 3 * line and height % line == 0, height
    lift = max(0, math.ceil((line - QFontMetricsF(label.font()).lineSpacing()) / 2))
    margins = label.contentsMargins()
    assert (margins.left(), margins.top(), margins.right(), margins.bottom()) == (0, -lift, 0, lift)

def test_a_message_row_opens_with_its_bold_lead_and_date():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import message_row, page
    from core.gui.widgets.marker import Marker
    when, now = datetime.datetime(2026, 10, 4, 12, 10), datetime.datetime(2026, 10, 6, 9, 0)

def test_a_message_row_sets_its_marker_and_sentence_by_the_table():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import message_row
    row = message_row.MessageRow("err", "A network named retrain already exists. Choose another name.", lead="Error")
    row.resize(300, row.heightForWidth(300))
    row.layout().activate()
    marker = row.marker
    at = marker.mapTo(row, QPoint(0, 0))
    assert (at.x(), at.y(), marker.width(), marker.height()) == (10, 4 + 3, 16, 16)
    assert (row.sentence.x(), row.sentence.y()) == (10 + 16 + 10, 4)
    assert row.sentence.x() + row.sentence.width() == 300
    line = SENTENCE_LINES[row.sentence.font().pixelSize()]
    assert row.sentence.height() % line == 0 and row.height() == 4 + row.sentence.height() + 4
    bare = message_row.MessageRow("", "An explanation.")
    bare.resize(300, bare.heightForWidth(300))
    bare.layout().activate()
    assert bare.sentence.x() == 10

def test_an_error_row_has_an_edge_of_whole_pixels_and_no_ground():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import message_row
    for dark in (False, True):
        with theme(dark):
            err, ground = design.colour("err").rgb(), design.colour("paper")
            for ratio, wanted in ((1, 2), (1.25, 2), (1.5, 3), (2, 4)):
                for kind in ("err", "warn", "info", "fine", ""):
                    row = message_row.MessageRow(kind, "A sentence long enough to wrap in a narrow row.", lead="Lead")
                    row.resize(300, row.heightForWidth(300))
                    image = _screen_of(row, ratio, ground)
                    for y in (0, image.height() // 2, int(row.height() * ratio) - 1):
                        run = 0
                        while image.pixel(run, y) == err:
                            run += 1
                        assert run == (wanted if kind == "err" else 0), (dark, ratio, kind, y, run)
                        assert image.pixel(round(5 * ratio), y) == ground.rgb(), (dark, ratio, kind, y)
