```python
def test_a_page_lines_up_what_stays_and_what_scrolls():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import page
    def margins(of):
        m = of.box.contentsMargins()
        return m.left(), m.top(), m.right(), m.bottom()
    made = page.Page()
    assert margins(made) == (22 - 4, 20, 20 - 4, 14) and made.box.spacing() == 0
    assert made.first_focus() is None and not made.is_small()
    head = page.PageHead("Train a network", "Simulates the recordings, then fits the network to them.")
    body, foot = _least(height=2000), QPushButton("Start training")
    made.add_fixed(head)
    made.add_gap(22, 14)
    scroller = made.add_scrolling(body)
    made.add_fixed(foot)
    assert isinstance(scroller, page.Scroller) and scroller.body is body
    at = lambda widget: widget.mapTo(made, QPoint(0, 0))
    made.resize(1000, 600)
    made.grab()
    assert at(head).x() == at(body).x() == at(foot).x() == 22 and at(head).y() == 20
    assert at(head).x() + head.width() == at(foot).x() + foot.width() == 1000 - 20
    assert at(foot).y() + foot.height() == 600 - 14
    assert scroller.y() - (at(head).y() + head.height()) == 22
    made.set_small(True)
    made.grab()
    assert made.is_small() and margins(made) == (16 - 4, 16, 14 - 4, 14) and head.sentence.isHidden()
    assert at(head).x() == at(body).x() == at(foot).x() == 16
    assert scroller.y() - (at(head).y() + head.height()) == 14
    made.set_small(False)
    made.grab()
    assert margins(made) == (22 - 4, 20, 20 - 4, 14) and not head.sentence.isHidden()
    assert scroller.y() - (at(head).y() + head.height()) == 22

def test_a_scroller_keeps_the_rings_room_and_is_a_tab_stop_only_while_it_scrolls():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import page
    class Told(QWidget):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__()
            self.fits = []
            self.setMinimumHeight(900)
        def fit(self, width):
            self.fits.append(width)
    def room(of):
        m = of.widget().layout().contentsMargins()
        return m.left(), m.top(), m.right(), m.bottom()
    before = sum(isinstance(w, page.Scroller) for w in QApplication.topLevelWidgets())      # the scrollers that are nobody's child
    body = Told()
    scroller = page.Scroller(body)
    assert scroller.frameShape() == QFrame.Shape.NoFrame and scroller.widgetResizable()
    assert scroller.horizontalScrollBarPolicy() == Qt.ScrollBarPolicy.ScrollBarAlwaysOff
    assert scroller.property("ring") == "inset" and scroller.body is body
    assert scroller.focusPolicy() == Qt.FocusPolicy.NoFocus and room(scroller) == (4, 0, 4, 4)
    scroller.resize(500, 300)
    scroller.grab()
    assert scroller.verticalScrollBar().maximum() > 0 and body.mapTo(scroller, QPoint(0, 0)).x() == 4
    assert scroller.focusPolicy() == Qt.FocusPolicy.TabFocus and room(scroller) == (4, 0, 4 + 2, 4)
    assert body.fits and set(body.fits) == {500 - 2 * 4 - 8 - 2}
    scroller.resize(500, 1200)
    scroller.grab()
    assert scroller.verticalScrollBar().maximum() == 0 and body.width() == 500 - 2 * 4
    assert scroller.focusPolicy() == Qt.FocusPolicy.NoFocus and room(scroller) == (4, 0, 4, 4)
    silent = page.Scroller(QWidget())          # a body that offers no fit() is held all the same
    silent.resize(300, 200)
    silent.grab()
    columns = page.Columns(QWidget(), QWidget())
    holder = page.Scroller(columns)
    holder.resize(940 + 2 * 4 + 8 + 2 - 1, 300)
    holder.grab()
    assert columns.stacked()
    holder.resize(940 + 2 * 4 + 8 + 2, 300)
    holder.grab()
    assert not columns.stacked()
    del scroller, silent, holder, columns, body
    assert sum(isinstance(w, page.Scroller) for w in QApplication.topLevelWidgets()) == before, "a scroller with no parent outlived its last name"

def test_two_columns_stack_below_940_or_below_their_own_least_widths():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets import page
    left, right = _least(100), _least(100)

    assert own.box.spacing() == 14

def test_a_page_with_nothing_selected_and_no_main_action_shows_no_accent():
    """A page of the shared devices under one theme's palette and sheet: a heading with two ordinary buttons and
    a middle of message rows. It has no words, so no pixel read is a letter's. The accent stands for what is
    selected, what is now and the main action; this page has none of the three, so no pixel of it or its tint."""
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui import paint
    from core.gui.widgets import message_row, page
    # every marker but "now", which is the accent's own; the error row first, where a low page still shows it
    kinds = ["err"] + [kind for kind in paint.MARKERS if kind not in ("err", "now")] + [""]
    assert len(kinds) == 10
    for dark in (False, True):
        with _the_look(dark):
            made = page.Page()
            try:
                head = page.PageHead("")
                head.add_action(QPushButton())
                head.add_action(QPushButton())
                middle = QWidget()
                rows = QVBoxLayout(middle)
                for kind in kinds:
                    rows.addWidget(message_row.MessageRow(kind, ""))
                made.add_fixed(head)
                made.add_gap(22, 14)
                scroller = made.add_scrolling(middle)
                bar = scroller.verticalScrollBar()
                paper, err = design.colour("paper"), design.colour("err").rgb()
                accent, tint = design.colour("accent").rgb(), design.colour("accent_tint").rgb()
                for height, scrolls in ((640, False), (220, True)):      # every row in sight; then too low for them
                    made.resize(360, height)
                    made.grab()
                    assert (bar.maximum() > 0) is scrolls, (dark, height, bar.maximum())
                    track = bar.mapTo(made, QPoint(bar.width() // 2, bar.height() - 3))     # under the handle
                    for ratio in (1, 1.25, 1.5, 2):
                        image = _screen_of(made, ratio, paper)
                        seen = _pixels(image)
                        assert err in seen, (dark, height, ratio, "the rows were not drawn")
                        if scrolls:                                  # only the sheet paints a scroll bar's track so
                            assert _at(image, track.x(), track.y()) == design.hex_colour("margin"), (dark, ratio)
                        assert not {accent, tint} & seen, (dark, height, ratio)
            finally:
                _gone(made)

def test_the_book_face_is_reached_only_from_its_places():
    """The book face has four places and no fifth. One label class asks the font factory for it, and only the
    modules of those places may build that label or ask the factory themselves; none may name a book face."""
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    missing = [name for name in BOOK_FACE_MODULES if not (root / name).is_file()]
    assert not missing, f"a module allowed the book face does not exist: {missing}"
    users, strays = set(), []
    for path in sorted((root / "core" / "gui").rglob("*.py")):
        rel = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()
        for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                callee = node.func
                name = getattr(callee, "id", None) or getattr(callee, "attr", "")
                if name == "Sentence" or (name == "book" and rel != "core/gui/fonts.py"):
                    users.add(rel)
                    if rel not in BOOK_FACE_MODULES:
                        strays.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} calls {name}()")
            elif (isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, str) and node.value in design.BOOK_FACES
                  and rel not in ("core/gui/design.py", "core/gui/fonts.py")):
                strays.append(f"{rel}:{node.lineno} names {node.value!r}")
    assert not strays, "the book face is reached outside its places:\n" + "\n".join(strays)
    unused = sorted(set(BOOK_FACE_MODULES) - users)
    assert not unused, f"allowed the book face and not using it: {unused}"
```

```python
    def _markup(self) -> str:
        if not self._text and not self._lead:
            return ""
        style = f"line-height:{self._line}px; white-space:pre-wrap"
        if self._quiet:
            style += f"; color:{design.hex_colour('ink_2')}"
        lead = ""
        if self._lead:
            lead_style = f"font-weight:{self._bold}"
            if self._quiet:
                lead_style += f"; color:{design.hex_colour('ink')}"
            lead = f"<span style='{lead_style}'>{html.escape(self._lead, quote=False)}</span>"
        body = html.escape(self._text, quote=False)
        return f"<p style='{style}'>{lead}{' ' if lead and body else ''}{body}</p>"
```

  ```python
  def _end_editing(field, leave=False):
      """The two ways editing ends: Enter, or the keyboard focus leaving by Tab."""
      if leave:
          QApplication.sendEvent(field, QFocusEvent(QEvent.FocusOut, Qt.TabFocusReason))
      else:
          QTest.keyClick(field, Qt.Key_Return)


  def _held_under_the_sheet(dark, *widgets):
      """A holder that carries the built sheet itself and is laid out without ever being shown, so the
      application's own sheet, its active window and its keyboard focus are never touched."""
      holder = QWidget()
      holder.setStyleSheet(design.build_qss(dark))
      column = QVBoxLayout(holder)
      for widget in widgets:
          column.addWidget(widget)
      column.addStretch(1)
      holder.resize(400, 200)
      holder.grab()                                    # polishes and lays out; nothing reaches a screen
      return holder


  def _holder_picture(holder, ratio=1.0):
      """The holder painted into a picture at a display scaling, after any layout its widgets have asked
      for since the last one. No painter is held here: the toolkit makes and ends its own."""
      picture = _image(holder.width(), holder.height(), ratio)
      holder.render(picture)
      return picture


  def test_typing_20480000_into_a_grouped_whole_number_field_shows_20_480_000():

      for digit in "20480000":
          QTest.keyClicks(field, digit)
          seen.append(field.text())
      assert seen == ["2", "20", "204", "2,048", "20,480", "204,800", "2,048,000", "20,480,000"]
      assert (field.value(), field.value_or_none(), field.plain_text()) == (20480000, 20480000, "20480000")
      field.setCursorPosition(2)                       # after the second digit: the caret keeps its place

      plain = IntField()                               # grouping is asked for; it is not the default
      QTest.keyClicks(plain, "20480000")
      assert (plain.text(), plain.value(), plain.isUndoAvailable()) == ("20480000", 20480000, True)

      assert IntField(" 12 ").text() == " 12 " and IntField(" 12 ").value_or_none() == 12
  ```

- [ ] **Step 3: Build the two fields** in `core/gui/widgets/labeled_inputs.py`. `QDoubleValidator` and `QIntValidator` leave the file; `import re`, `from PySide6.QtCore import Qt, Signal`, `QValidator` (from `PySide6.QtGui`) and `from ..style import set_class` come in. The three rules and the one algorithm the tests do not spell out:
  ```python
  COMMA_SENTENCE = "Use a point as the decimal sign."
  _WHOLE = re.compile(r"-?(?:[0-9]+|[0-9]{1,3}(?:,[0-9]{3})+)")     # read: digits, or commas where grouping puts them
  _WHOLE_KEYS = re.compile(r"-?[0-9]*")                             # typed, once its commas are taken out
  _DECIMAL_KEYS = re.compile(r"[+-]?[0-9,]*\.?[0-9,]*(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]*)?")   # typed: a comma shows, a second point does not

      def _edited(self, text):                         # IntField: connected to textEdited (the user's edits only)
          caret = self.cursorPosition()
          kept = text.replace(",", "")
          before = sum(ch != "," for ch in text[:caret])                # the minus counts; a comma does not
          if self._grouped:
              sign = "-" if kept.startswith("-") else ""
              digits = kept[len(sign):]
              shown = sign + (f"{int(digits):,}" if digits else "")
          else:
              shown = kept
          pos = 0
          while pos < len(shown) and before > 0:
              before -= shown[pos] != ","
              pos += 1
          if self._forward and shown[caret:caret + 1] == "," and shown[:caret] + shown[caret + 1:] == text:
              pos = caret + 1                          # Delete took a comma only: step over it, so the next takes a digit
          if shown != text:
              QLineEdit.setText(self, shown)           # not self.setText: that one is for text set from code
          self.setCursorPosition(pos)
  ```
  The rest, by contract:
  - `_whole(text)`: `int(text.strip().replace(",", ""))` when `_WHOLE.fullmatch(text.strip())`, else `None`. No plus: neither `_WHOLE` nor `_WHOLE_KEYS` takes one (the whole-number field keeps digits and a leading minus, and nothing else); `_DECIMAL_KEYS` does, for a decimal field.
  - `_WholeKeys.validate(self, text, pos)`: `Acceptable` when `_WHOLE_KEYS.fullmatch(text.replace(",", ""))`, else `Invalid`; `_DecimalKeys.validate`: the same on `_DECIMAL_KEYS.fullmatch(text)`. Both return `(state, text, pos)` with the text and the position unchanged, and neither defines a fix-up.

```python
ASK_MARKERS = ("warn", "err", "info")   # the three a question may carry; not the ten states of the paint module
ITEMS_SHOWN = 8                    # a list longer than this scrolls inside the question
DETAIL_LINES = 12                  # the height of the full error, in lines of console text
CANCEL = "Cancel"                  # the safe answer of the form that asks for a line of text
FULL_ERROR = "Show the full error"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Wording:
    """What a question says, as plain words: readable after the dialog itself is gone."""
    title: str; sentence: str; safe: str; other: str | None; loses_work: bool; marker: str
    items: tuple[str, ...]; beneath: str; detail: str; label: str | None      # "" for no closing lines, no error

class Ask(QDialog):
    wording: Wording; answer_text: str | None      # the line of text, kept when the other answer is taken
    marker: Marker; sentence: Sentence; beneath: Sentence | None; items_area: QScrollArea | None
    safe_button: QPushButton; other_button: QPushButton | None; field: QLineEdit | None
    field_message: QLabel | None; detail_link: QPushButton | None; detail_box: QPlainTextEdit | None
    def __init__(self, parent, title: str, sentence: str, safe: str, other: str | None = None, *,
                 loses_work: bool = False, marker: str = "warn", items: Sequence[str] | None = None,
                 beneath: str | None = None, detail: str | None = None, label: str | None = None,
                 text: str = "", check: Callable[[str], str | None] | None = None) -> None: ...

def ask(parent, title: str, sentence: str, safe: str, other: str | None = None, *, loses_work: bool = False,
        marker: str = "warn", items: Sequence[str] | None = None, beneath: str | None = None,
        detail: str | None = None) -> bool: ...                      # True for the other answer, False for the safe one

def ask_text(parent, title: str, sentence: str, label: str, other: str, *, text: str = "",
             check: Callable[[str], str | None] | None = None, items=None, beneath=None) -> str | None: ...
                                                                     # the line, stripped, for the other answer; None for "Cancel"
```

- **The rules of `tests/test_look.py`** (the plan's head has them all; these are the ones this task can break). One application serves the whole gate and this file is collected before six window suites, so nothing may be left behind.
  1. The application object first: every test that builds a widget begins `QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])`, before anything else (in a one-file run nothing else has made the application, and a widget built without one ends the process).

  3. Letting a widget go: a dialog that was shown is closed and handed to Task 14's `_gone` (`_question_closed`); a dialog that was never shown is held in a name only and goes when the name is dropped. Never a bare `deleteLater()` in a test (measured again for this section: five dialogs shown, closed, asked to delete themselves later and dropped were all five still top-level widgets; closed and dropped, or handed to `_gone`, none was), never a flush for every receiver (trap 15).

  6. The new module joins `LOOK_MODULES`; no fresh-interpreter test of this task's own.

```python
# the shared question
import ast
from pathlib import Path

from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent, QPoint, QSize, Qt
from PySide6.QtGui import QFocusEvent, QGuiApplication, QKeyEvent
from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QDialog, QLabel, QPlainTextEdit, QWidget

A_QUESTION = ("Stop training?", "The simulations are kept. The fit so far will be lost.", "Keep training")
A_TRACEBACK = "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  ...\nRuntimeError: it failed"

def _question_opened(dialog):
    """Opened without blocking, without reaching a screen and without being activated, with the list its answer
    lands in. It is shown, because a dialog hands Enter to its default button only while that button is visible."""
    dialog.setAttribute(Qt.WidgetAttribute.WA_DontShowOnScreen, True)
    dialog.setAttribute(Qt.WidgetAttribute.WA_ShowWithoutActivating, True)
    got = []
    dialog.finished.connect(got.append)
    dialog.show()
    QApplication.processEvents()
    return dialog, got

def _question_closed(dialog):
    """Closed and deleted now. A modal dialog left open, or one only asked to delete itself later, would stay
    for every test that runs after this one."""
    dialog.close()
    _gone(dialog)

def _question_key(target, key):
    for kind in (QEvent.Type.KeyPress, QEvent.Type.KeyRelease):
        QApplication.sendEvent(target, QKeyEvent(kind, key, Qt.KeyboardModifier.NoModifier,
                                                 " " if key == Qt.Key.Key_Space else ""))
    QApplication.processEvents()

def _question_focus(old, new):
    """What the Tab key does to two controls: the focus leaves one and arrives at the other."""
    QApplication.sendEvent(old, QFocusEvent(QEvent.Type.FocusOut, Qt.FocusReason.TabFocusReason))
    QApplication.sendEvent(new, QFocusEvent(QEvent.Type.FocusIn, Qt.FocusReason.TabFocusReason))
    QApplication.processEvents()

def _in_question(widget):
    """Where a control of a question stands, from the question's own top left corner."""
    return widget.mapTo(widget.window(), QPoint(0, 0))

def test_a_question_takes_enter_escape_and_its_close_button_as_the_safe_answer():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    keys = (Qt.Key.Key_Return, Qt.Key.Key_Enter, Qt.Key.Key_Escape, Qt.Key.Key_Space, None)   # None: the frame's close
    for other, loses_work in (("Stop and lose the fit", True), ("Go on", False), (None, False)):
        for on_other in ((False, True) if other else (False,)):
            for key in keys:
                dialog, got = _question_opened(Ask(None, *A_QUESTION, other, loses_work=loses_work))
                try:
                    if on_other:
                        _question_focus(dialog.safe_button, dialog.other_button)
                    assert dialog.safe_button.isDefault(), "the default left the safe answer when the focus moved"
                    if key is None:
                        dialog.close()
                    else:
                        _question_key(dialog.other_button if on_other else dialog.safe_button, key)
                    pressed_it = on_other and key == Qt.Key.Key_Space      # the space bar presses what has the focus
                    assert got == [1 if pressed_it else 0], (other, on_other, key, got)
                finally:
                    _question_closed(dialog)
    assert Ask(None, *A_QUESTION).other_button is None, "with no other answer a question tells: one button"

def test_a_question_is_a_modal_dialog_set_out_by_the_table_and_grows_with_the_text_size():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    from core.gui.widgets.page import Sentence
    assert design.DIALOG == {"w": 448, "pad": (20, 16, 20, 18), "gap": 16, "marker": 24, "marker_gap": 14,
                             "marker_drop": 1}
    host = QWidget()
    for factor, wide in ((1.0, 448), (1.25, 560)):
        with text_size(factor):
            left, top, right, bottom, mark, gap, drop = (design.scaled(n) for n in (20, 16, 20, 18, 24, 14, 1))
            dialog, _got = _question_opened(Ask(host, *A_QUESTION, "Go on"))
            try:
                marker, sentence, safe, other = dialog.marker, dialog.sentence, dialog.safe_button, dialog.other_button
                assert dialog.width() == wide == design.scaled(448), (factor, dialog.width())
                at = _in_question(marker)
                assert (at.x(), at.y(), marker.width(), marker.height()) == (left, top + drop, mark, mark)
                assert isinstance(sentence, Sentence) and sentence.plain_text() == A_QUESTION[1]
                assert (_in_question(sentence).x(), _in_question(sentence).y()) == (left + mark + gap, top)
                assert _in_question(sentence).x() + sentence.width() == wide - right
                assert _in_question(safe).x() + safe.width() == wide - right and _in_question(other).x() == left
                assert _in_question(safe).y() + safe.height() == dialog.height() - bottom
                flags = dialog.windowFlags()
                assert isinstance(dialog, QDialog) and dialog.windowTitle() == "Stop training?" and dialog.isModal()
                assert flags & Qt.WindowType.WindowTitleHint and flags & Qt.WindowType.WindowCloseButtonHint
                assert not flags & Qt.WindowType.FramelessWindowHint and dialog.parent() is host
                assert dialog.windowModality() == Qt.WindowModality.WindowModal
            finally:
                _question_closed(dialog)
    assert Ask(None, *A_QUESTION).windowModality() == Qt.WindowModality.ApplicationModal

def test_nine_items_scroll_inside_the_question_and_none_is_cut():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    from core.gui.widgets.page import Sentence
    assert design.text_scale() == 1.0, "a text factor leaked into this suite"
    long = "a simulation set whose name goes on for longer than one line of the question can hold, " * 2
    for count in (1, 8, 9, 14):
        items = [f"simulation set number {n}" for n in range(count - 1)] + [long]
        dialog, got = _question_opened(Ask(None, *A_QUESTION, "Go on", items=items, beneath="Each stays in Records."))
        try:
            area = dialog.items_area
            rows, bar, view = area.widget().findChildren(Sentence), area.verticalScrollBar(), area.viewport()
            line = SENTENCE_LINES[rows[0].font().pixelSize()]      # 22, in a book face or in the lettering at its size
            assert [row.plain_text() for row in rows] == items, "one item to a line, in order, as written"
            heights = [row.height() for row in rows]
            assert heights == [row.heightForWidth(row.width()) for row in rows], "an item is cut short"
            assert all(row.x() + row.width() <= view.width() for row in rows), "an item runs under the scroll bar"
            assert area.horizontalScrollBar().maximum() == 0 and heights[-1] >= 2 * line and set(heights[:-1]) <= {line}
            assert rows[-1].y() + heights[-1] == area.widget().height() == sum(heights)
            assert area.width() == dialog.sentence.width() and dialog.width() == 448
            assert not view.autoFillBackground() and not area.widget().autoFillBackground()
            under_the_sentence = _in_question(dialog.sentence).y() + dialog.sentence.height() + 12
            assert _in_question(area).y() == under_the_sentence, "the list stands 12 under the sentence"
            assert _in_question(dialog.beneath).y() == under_the_sentence + area.height() + 12, "and the closing lines 12 under it"
            if count <= 8:
                assert area.height() == sum(heights) and bar.maximum() == 0
                assert area.focusPolicy() == Qt.FocusPolicy.NoFocus
            else:
                assert area.height() == 8 * line and bar.maximum() == sum(heights) - area.height()
                assert area.focusPolicy() == Qt.FocusPolicy.TabFocus and area.property("ring") == "inset"
                _question_key(area, Qt.Key.Key_Down)
                assert got == [], "an arrow key in the list answered the question"
                _question_key(area, Qt.Key.Key_Return)
                assert got == [0], "Enter with the list in focus did not mean the safe answer"
        finally:
            _question_closed(dialog)
    assert Ask(None, *A_QUESTION).items_area is None and Ask(None, *A_QUESTION, items=[]).items_area is None

def test_a_question_that_asks_for_a_line_of_text_takes_enter_only_once_the_text_holds():
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    said, taken = [], "A plan named retrain already exists. Choose another name."

    def check(text):
        said.append(text)
        return taken if text == "retrain" else None

    def form(text="", judge=check):
        return _question_opened(Ask(None, "Save as a plan", "Only the settings that differ from their usual values are written.",
                                    "Cancel", "Save this plan", marker="info", label="Plan name", text=text, check=judge))

    def enter_on_cancel(asking):
        _question_focus(asking.field, asking.safe_button)
        _question_key(asking.safe_button, Qt.Key.Key_Return)

    dialog, got = form()
    try:
        field, save, cancel, wrong = dialog.field, dialog.other_button, dialog.safe_button, dialog.field_message
        assert save.isDefault() and save.property("cls") == "primary" and cancel.property("cls") is None
        assert not save.isEnabled() and not wrong.isVisible() and said == []
        assert _in_question(field).y() >= _in_question(dialog.sentence).y() + dialog.sentence.height() + 12
        assert _in_question(field).x() > _in_question(dialog.sentence).x(), "the label stands to the left of its field"
        _question_key(field, Qt.Key.Key_Return)
        assert got == [] and dialog.isVisible(), "Enter threw an empty line away"
        field.setText("   ")
        assert not save.isEnabled() and said == [], "a blank line was judged"
        field.setText(" retrain ")
        assert said == ["retrain"] and not save.isEnabled() and field.property("state") == "error"
        assert wrong.isVisible() and wrong.text() == taken and wrong.textFormat() == Qt.TextFormat.PlainText
        _question_key(field, Qt.Key.Key_Return)
        _question_key(field, Qt.Key.Key_Enter)
        assert got == [] and dialog.answer_text is None, "Enter took a line that does not hold"
        field.setText(" retrain 2 ")
        assert save.isEnabled() and field.property("state") != "error" and not wrong.isVisible()
        _question_key(field, Qt.Key.Key_Return)
        assert got == [1] and dialog.answer_text == "retrain 2"
    finally:
        _question_closed(dialog)
    for leave in (lambda asking: _question_key(asking.field, Qt.Key.Key_Escape), lambda asking: asking.close(),
                  lambda asking: _question_key(asking.safe_button, Qt.Key.Key_Space), enter_on_cancel):
        dialog, got = form("old name")
        try:
            assert dialog.other_button.isEnabled() and dialog.field.text() == "old name"
            leave(dialog)
            assert got == [0] and dialog.answer_text is None
        finally:
            _question_closed(dialog)
    dialog, got = form(judge=None)                                # with nothing to judge it, any line that is not blank holds
    try:
        assert not dialog.other_button.isEnabled()
        dialog.field.setText("anything")
        _question_key(dialog.field, Qt.Key.Key_Return)
        assert got == [1] and dialog.answer_text == "anything"
    finally:
        _question_closed(dialog)

def test_a_question_shows_its_words_as_written():
    """A record's name may hold a brace, an ampersand or an angle bracket. No text handed to a question is read
    as markup: three of its places are the sentence label, which shows what it is given; the full error is plain
    console text; the label of the line of text and what is wrong with the line are plain-text labels. A button,
    and a label that names a field, read a single ampersand in their words as the mark of an access key: they
    leave it out and take the key. So the two answers and that label are handed their words with each ampersand
    doubled, which shows one and takes no key, and the question keeps the words as its caller wrote them."""
    QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    from core.gui.widgets.page import Sentence
    odd = 'Set {name} to <b>3 & 4</b>, not {0}; "two  spaces".'
    telling = Ask(None, "Error", odd, "OK", marker="err", items=[odd, "a second item"], beneath=odd,
                  detail=odd + "\n  " + odd)
    for label in (telling.sentence, telling.items_area.widget().findChildren(Sentence)[0], telling.beneath):
        assert isinstance(label, Sentence) and label.plain_text() == odd, "a text was changed on its way to its label"
        assert "<b>" not in label.text() and "&lt;b&gt;" in label.text(), "a text was read as markup"
    assert telling.detail_box.toPlainText() == odd + "\n  " + odd and telling.wording.sentence == odd
    answers = ("Keep & close", "Stop & lose <it>")
    asking = Ask(None, "Save as a plan", odd, *answers, marker="info", label=odd, text=odd, check=lambda text: odd)
    for button, words in zip((asking.safe_button, asking.other_button), answers):
        assert button.text() == words.replace("&", "&&"), "an answer would be shown without its ampersand"
        assert button.shortcut().isEmpty(), "an answer took an access key from its words"
    assert (asking.wording.safe, asking.wording.other, asking.wording.label) == (*answers, odd)
    named = [label for label in asking.findChildren(QLabel) if label.buddy() is asking.field]
    assert [label.text() for label in named] == [odd.replace("&", "&&")], "one label names the field, shown as written"
    assert named[0].textFormat() == Qt.TextFormat.PlainText
    assert asking.field.text() == odd and asking.field_message.text() == odd
    assert asking.field_message.textFormat() == Qt.TextFormat.PlainText

def test_the_question_opens_only_through_the_call_the_suites_stand_on():
    """The suites replace the question class's own ``exec`` for the whole session, because a dialog nobody
    answers would otherwise open and never close. So the module opens its dialog in exactly two places, each
    ``dialog.exec()`` looked up on the dialog when it runs; the class defines no opening call of its own; the
    dialog is never told to delete itself on closing, since its answer is read after it has closed; and the
    module costs the toolkit and the look's own modules, nothing that names a control or loads the engine."""
    from core.gui.widgets import ask as module
    opening, found, imported = ("exec", "exec_", "open"), [], set()
    for top in ast.parse(Path(module.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")).body:
        for node in ast.walk(top):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and node.attr in opening + ("WA_DeleteOnClose",):
                found.append((getattr(top, "name", ""), ast.unparse(node)))
            elif isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)) and node.name in opening:
                found.append((getattr(top, "name", ""), f"def {node.name}"))
            elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
                imported |= {alias.name for alias in node.names}
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom) and not node.level:
                imported.add(node.module)
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
                base = ("core.gui.widgets", "core.gui")[node.level - 1]
                imported |= {f"{base}.{node.module}"} if node.module else {f"{base}.{alias.name}" for alias in node.names}
    assert found == [("ask", "dialog.exec"), ("ask_text", "dialog.exec")], found
    assert imported <= {"collections.abc", "dataclasses", "PySide6.QtCore", "PySide6.QtGui", "PySide6.QtWidgets",
                        "core.gui.design", "core.gui.fonts", "core.gui.style", "core.gui.widgets.marker",
                        "core.gui.widgets.page"}, imported
    assert (module.CANCEL, module.FULL_ERROR, module.ITEMS_SHOWN, module.DETAIL_LINES, module.ASK_MARKERS) == (
        "Cancel", "Show the full error", 8, 12, ("warn", "err", "info"))
```

```python
def _the_guard_stands_on_the_question():
    """Called before anything that could reach the question's ``exec``: a real one opens a dialog that nothing
    closes, which stalls the run where a failed assertion would only fail it."""
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QMessageBox
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import Ask
    guard = vars(QMessageBox).get("exec")
    assert guard is not None and vars(Ask).get("exec") is guard, (
        "the session guard does not stand on the question class, so its exec would open for real: "
        "tests/conftest.py::_no_modal_dialogs")


def _the_questions_let_go():
    """Carry out the deletion each question was asked for when it was answered. In the window the next turn
    of the event loop does it; no loop turns under the suites, so a question would stay, hidden, to the end
    of the run. Aimed at the dialogs this test opened and at nothing else in the process. Hands back how
    many there were, how many of them were still there before, and how many are after."""
    from PySide6.QtCore import QEvent
    from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication
    from shiboken6 import isValid
    from tests._fixtures import SHOWN
    dialogs = list(SHOWN)
    before = sum(isValid(dialog) for dialog in dialogs)
    for dialog in dialogs:
        QApplication.sendPostedEvents(dialog, QEvent.Type.DeferredDelete)
    return len(dialogs), before, sum(isValid(dialog) for dialog in dialogs)


def test_asked_reads_a_question_of_the_shared_class_into_the_same_record():
    """Each way of asking and telling, through the two calls every caller uses, read into the record a
    message box is read into. The words are kept at opening, so they outlive the dialog; and each call
    lets go of its dialog once it is answered, which in the window the next turn of the event loop
    carries out and here a flush aimed at these five dialogs alone."""
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import ask, ask_text
    from tests._fixtures import Asked, all_asked, asked, forget_asked

    qt_app()
    _the_guard_stands_on_the_question()
    tb = "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  ...\nRuntimeError: it failed"
    held, stays = ["the prior retrain_prior", "the posterior retrain"], "Each stays in Records and can be loaded again."
    forget_asked()
    assert ask(None, "Stop training?", "The fit so far will be lost.", "Keep training", "Stop and lose the fit",
               loses_work=True, items=held, beneath=stays) is False
    assert ask(None, "Check your inputs", "Batches must be at least 1.", "OK",
               beneath="Change it in the Batches field.") is False
    assert ask(None, "Error", "it failed", "OK", marker="err", detail=tb) is False
    assert ask(None, "A run is live", "Wait for it to end.", "OK", marker="info") is False
    assert ask_text(None, "Save as a plan", "Only what differs is written.", "Plan name", "Save this plan",
                    text="retrain", items=["batches = 5,000"]) is None
    assert _the_questions_let_go() == (5, 5, 0), "a call kept its dialog after it was answered"
    bare = dict(beneath="", items=(), detail="", loses_work=False)
    told = dict(answers=("OK",), default="OK", safe="OK")
    assert all_asked() == [
        Asked(kind="question", title="Stop training?", marker="warn", sentence="The fit so far will be lost.",
              beneath=stays, items=tuple(held), detail="", answers=("Stop and lose the fit", "Keep training"),
              default="Keep training", safe="Keep training", loses_work=True),
        Asked(kind="refusal", title="Check your inputs", marker="warn", sentence="Batches must be at least 1.",
              **{**bare, "beneath": "Change it in the Batches field."}, **told),
        Asked(kind="error", title="Error", marker="err", sentence="it failed", **{**bare, "detail": tb}, **told),
        Asked(kind="notice", title="A run is live", marker="info", sentence="Wait for it to end.", **bare, **told),
        Asked(kind="question", title="Save as a plan", marker="info", sentence="Only what differs is written.",
              answers=("Save this plan", "Cancel"), default="Save this plan", safe="Cancel",
              **{**bare, "items": ("batches = 5,000",)})]
    assert all_asked()[0].text == "\n".join([*held, stays]) and asked().text == "batches = 5,000"


def test_choose_answers_a_question_of_the_shared_class_and_types_its_line_of_text(monkeypatch):
    """An answer is a click on the question's own button; a line of text is typed into its field first.
    A question that does not offer what was chosen, or whose answer is greyed, is left unanswered. At the
    end every question these calls opened is gone."""
    from core.gui.widgets.ask import ask, ask_text
    from tests._fixtures import all_asked, choose, forget_asked

    qt_app()
    _the_guard_stands_on_the_question()

    def question():
        return ask(None, "Stop training?", "The fit so far will be lost.", "Keep training",
                   "Stop and lose the fit", loses_work=True)

    def telling():
        return ask(None, "Check your inputs", "Batches must be at least 1.", "OK")

    def line(start=""):
        return ask_text(None, "Save as a plan", "Only what differs is written.", "Plan name", "Save this plan",
                        text=start, check=lambda text: "That name is taken." if text == "retrain" else None)

    counts = []
    forget_asked()
    choose(monkeypatch, other=True, during=lambda: counts.append(len(all_asked())))
    assert question() is True and telling() is False, "one answer: there is no other"
    assert line() is None, "the other answer is greyed while the line is empty"
    assert line("retrain 2") == "retrain 2" and line("retrain") is None
    assert counts == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "recorded first, then `during`, then the click"
    choose(monkeypatch, other=True, text="  a new name  ")
    assert line() == "a new name" and line("old name") == "a new name" and question() is True
    choose(monkeypatch, other=True, text="retrain")
    assert line("a free name") is None, "a line that does not hold was handed back"
    for words, taken in (("Stop and lose the fit", True), ("Keep training", False), ("No such answer", False)):
        choose(monkeypatch, words=words)
        assert question() is taken and line("old name") is None, words
    choose(monkeypatch, words="Cancel", text="a new name")
    assert line() is None
    choose(monkeypatch, words="Save this plan", text="a new name")
    assert line() == "a new name" and question() is False, "a question does not offer the other form's answer"
    choose(monkeypatch, default=True)                     # Enter
    assert question() is False and telling() is False and line() is None and line("old name") == "old name"
    choose(monkeypatch, text="typed and left")            # nothing chosen: the unanswered guard again
    assert line() is None and question() is False
    before = len(all_asked())
    monkeypatch.undo()
    assert question() is False and line("old name") is None and len(all_asked()) == before + 2, \
        "the session guard must be back after the undo"
    opened, there, left = _the_questions_let_go()
    assert opened == there == len(all_asked()) and left == 0, "a question stayed behind after it was answered"
```

Plain words; in the order the work is done. "Nothing" means nothing changes on your screen or in how
PRISM behaves.

**Task 0. The starting test run, and pictures of today's window (I run it).**
You notice: nothing in PRISM. I tell you one line before the pictures and one after, and two sentences
at the end: the tests are green, and pictures of today's window are kept for comparison.
Choices you have not seen:
- For the pictures I build the real window, hidden, never on your screen. It uses scratch settings and
  an empty scratch record store, never yours. It reads the graphics card's free memory, as opening
  PRISM always does. I never do it while a run of yours is live.
- Before and after each test run I list your records folder (names, sizes, times; no file is opened),
  to see that nothing changed. How long that listing takes over your full simulation set is not known.
  If it is slow I keep it for the two runs of record and the picture runs.
- A test run will not start while any Python program is running on this computer.
- The picture recipe has never been run by anyone. This is its first run.

**Task 1. Tidying the tests, first part.**
You notice: nothing. No program file changes.
Choices you have not seen:

  whole run.
- The tests then run under five standing safeguards. The project's instructions say four. I put the
  corrected sentence to you at the end of the stage and change nothing before you agree.

  curves run ink, blue, vermilion, green, orange, sky blue, purple; the calibration's cumulative rank
  lines repeat seven colours where they had ten.
- Changing the appearance during a run no longer changes how its later figures look. Stored figures
  and figures already on screen are untouched. Figures from the command line are unchanged.
Choices you have not seen:
- Lines that name no width are a touch thinner (1.44 pt, were 1.5).
- A character that Inter lacks is drawn in a second face rather than as an empty box.
- No picture of this stage shows a figure. You see these on your own screen at the first run after the
  stage, and are told in words at the end.

**Task 12. One blue, one vermilion, one green, one orange (the one change to the engine).**
You notice: nothing in the window's own controls. In every figure the engine draws, from the window
and from the command line: blues become one blue, reds and crimson become vermilion, greens one green,
oranges one orange. The fitting library's own figures (the rank histogram, the coverage figure, the
grey bands) keep its dark red, pure blue and grey; PRISM's code cannot reach them.
Choices you have not seen:
- Which old colour goes to which of the four.
- The grey crosses of the predictive check (values with no variance) take the axis colour and lie on a
  zero line of that same colour: told apart by shape and legend only.
- The note "no finite posterior-predictive PSD" is in vermilion lettering.
- Blue, vermilion and green are nearly equal in lightness. They differ by hue alone, and not at all in
  a grey print.
- Orange on the white page is weak (2.25 to 1); today's oranges are between 1.97 and 2.53.
- No number, width, dash, marker or label changes; a check holds that.

**Task 13. Markers, small icons and the ruled line (built, on no screen).**
You notice: nothing.
Choices you have not seen (you meet them when a later stage uses the pieces):
- A greyed state marker keeps its inner mark (the tick, the cross) in the page's colour; only its
  shape greys. Greyed whole, four of the ten markers would read as plain discs.
- A marker greys with the form it stands in.
- The "up" arrowhead is the "down" one mirrored.
- A ruled line is always a whole number of screen pixels and never vanishes, at any display scaling.
- A section's heading can hold one small thing at its right end.

**Task 14. The three-rule table (built, on no screen).**
You notice: nothing.
Choices you have not seen:
- The sort arrow points up when the smallest value is first, down when the largest is.
- A value's unit is drawn one space after its figure.
- Tab leaves a table; the arrow keys move inside it.
- A header is sorted with the mouse only. A keyboard way to sort is left to the Records stage.
- Rows and header cells have no look under the pointer, and the table has no greyed look. Still yours
  to decide.

**Task 15. The time axis of a run (built, on no screen).**
You notice: nothing. You meet it when the run's page is built.
Choices you have not seen:
- An axis that runs late grows by as many whole days as it needs.
- The axis is never shorter than 30 seconds.
- An end with no earliest end reads as a firm end. No hatched key is shown beside a firm end.
- No seconds in the line under the axis.
- No tick and no label in the first 30 seconds of a run whose end is not known.
- A long "no end known" sentence is neither wrapped nor cut here.

**Task 16. Page pieces: the sentence, the message row, the page head (built, on no screen).**
You notice: nothing. Four pictures, made on the real screen with the window hidden, are the only view.
Choices you have not seen:
- A sentence shows its text exactly as written: two spaces, a line break, "<" and "&" are not tidied.
- A message with no marker starts at the row's ordinary left margin.
- The row writes the full stop after its bold opening word.
- A message row is not changed after it is built; a page with new facts builds new rows.

**Task 17. Number boxes and the drop-down.**
You notice (on today's forms; no picture shows it):
- In a box for a decimal number a typed comma now stays. The box gets a 2 px outline and its tool tip
  says "Use a point as the decimal sign." Until now 6,5 silently became 65.
- In a box for a whole number a typed comma no longer shows: 5,000 typed shows 5000. A "+" can no
  longer be typed. A number of more than ten digits can be typed.
- No comma appears in any whole number yet. No drop-down gets its arrow yet.
- One case to know before a long run: the memory-limit box. With 6,5 typed, today the limit silently
  becomes 65 GiB. After this task the box is outlined and the limit reads 0, which means "off",
  exactly as a blank box does today. The note under the box says what is in force.
Choices you have not seen:
- On today's forms the error sentence is in the tool tip only. The line under the box comes with the
  first rebuilt form.
- A whole number that today's build saved with its commas (5,000 left in a box, refused at every
  click) now reads 5000 and is saved back as 5000. A saved "+5" comes back as "+5" and is refused.
- A paste holding anything but digits, commas and a leading minus is refused whole.
- In the model builder's decimal boxes a typed 6,5 is 65 today; afterwards it reads 0 beside an
  outlined box.

**Task 18. The shared question dialog (built, on no screen; no box is replaced).**
You notice: nothing. A few pictures, made hidden on the real screen, are the first view.
Choices you have not seen (each shows when a later stage first asks through it):
- The form that asks for a line of text: its main answer is the accent button at the left, "Cancel" at
  the right. Enter means the main answer unless the focus is on "Cancel". The line is handed back
  without leading or trailing spaces. A blank line is never judged.
- The full error: its link is pressed with the mouse or the space bar. Once opened it stays open,
  twelve lines high.
- A list is as tall as its first eight items and scrolls from the ninth.
- A very long sentence is not cut. At about 1,000 characters with a long list the answers could fall
  below a small screen's edge. A single word longer than the text column is cut at the right edge.
- An "&" in an answer is shown as written and makes no keyboard shortcut.
- In dark an ordinary answer stands one shade darker than the question's ground until a later stage
  adds the rule.

**Task 19. The exit (I run it).**
You notice: nothing new in PRISM. You get the pictures (plain, at 150 % text size, at 150 % display
scaling). You are asked twice to leave the graphics card alone (the pictures; the slow tests, about 75
minutes). You are told in plain words what no picture shows: the wheel over a drop-down, a comma typed
in a number box, a "+" no longer typed, the ring's rules, and the changes to figures. You are asked one
question: whether two sentences of the project's instructions may be corrected (five safeguards, not
four; twenty-three test suites, not twenty-two).
Choices you have not seen: none beyond the above. Passages of the guide that this stage makes out of
date are left for the stage that rewrites the guide, and listed.
